title: Ambipolar Electrochemical Doping of CsPbBr 3 Nanocrystals
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electronic doping underpins many semiconductor applications but has remained elusive for lead halide perovskite nanocrystals because their high density and low formation energy of defects easily compensate introduced dopants. Here, we use electrochemical doping as a strategy to avoid doping compensation. Electrochemical injection of electrons or holes into the nanocrystal is compensated by surface-adsorbed electrolyte counterions, therefore not compromising crystal structure. We accomplished ambipolar (n- and p-type) doped CsPbBr3 nanocrystals with charge carrier concentrations ranging from intrinsic up to 4.8 × 1017 cm–3 (corresponding to 0.25 charges per nanocrystal). We show that electrochemical doping is reversible and stable at these free carrier concentrations. The extent of doping and stability are enabled by the use of lecithin, a zwitterionic ligand that strongly binds to the surface of the CsPbBr3 nanocrystals while still allowing ion and electron transfer. Lecithin stabilizes the surface atoms by shifting the potentials for Pb2+ reduction and Br– oxidation outside of the bandgap. The inferred surface-chemistry design rules for stable electrochemical doping can also serve as a guideline for developing CsPbBr3 nanocrystals stable under high free-carrier concentrations in optoelectronic devices, such as light-emitting diodes or electronically triggered quantum light sources.

title: CHARMM-Compatible Molecular Mechanics Force Fields for Multiscale Modeling of HIV-1 Replication Inhibitors
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molecular dynamics simulations provide insight into inhibitor-protein interactions and support rational drug design; however, their accuracy depends on reliable molecular mechanics force field parameters and coarse-grained representations that retain relevant molecular features. Although force field parameter sets for biomacromolecules are well established, the chemical diversity of small-molecule inhibitors often requires the development of system-specific parameters. Here, we present a parametrization framework integrating quantum mechanical optimization, experimental benchmarking, and small-molecule coarse-graining, demonstrated using HIV-1 inhibitors targeting multiple stages of the viral replication cycle. We provide a curated data set of CHARMM-compatible force field parameters for 12 HIV-1 inhibitors and the HIV assembly cofactor inositol hexakisphosphate (IP6), together with geometry-optimized atomic structures and ligand restraint files. The resulting parameters are validated against experimental structural and thermodynamic benchmarks, including lenacapavir binding free energy estimates, through inhibitor-bound complex simulations. We demonstrate applications of the parameter data set by quantifying inhibitor-protein interactions, including the free-energy profile of an integrase strand transfer inhibitor interacting with the viral capsid lattice, and the binding energetics of an allosteric integrase inhibitor. Furthermore, we extend the all-atom inhibitor parameter data set through a novel coarse-graining strategy for small molecules that preserves key electrostatic features. The HIV-1 inhibitor force field parameter data set is a publicly available resource that establishes a unified framework for multiscale modeling of HIV-1 inhibitors and facilitates computational and structural biology studies of drug resistance and inhibitor design. More generally, the framework presented here is broadly applicable to small-molecule parametrization and multiscale simulations in other therapeutic and biomolecular contexts.

title: Melting and resistivity of iron at Earth core conditions using pulsed Joule heating
abstract: The melting temperature and electrical resistivity of iron at high pressure are essential for understanding Earth’s core. Here we use a new high-pressure method – microsecond pulsed Joule heating in diamond anvil cells – to identify melting and measure resistivity of solid and liquid iron. More than 300 reproducible melting measurements indicate a surprisingly shallow melting curve, reaching 6 K/GPa and 4160 ± 80 K at 200 GPa. Extrapolating in pressure and iron alloy composition, and combining with our 76 μ Ω cm measurement of liquid iron’s resistivity, we infer a relatively cold core-mantle boundary (3430 K) with a low adiabatic outer core heat flow (9.8 TW). This suggests thermal convection alone could have powered the geodynamo prior to inner core formation and that today’s lowermost mantle is fully solid.

title: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy for proton exchange membrane fuel cells: From implementation to application
abstract: Hydrogen fuel cells play a vital role in achieving a hydrogen-powered, carbon-neutral society. Despite being deployed in various stationary and transportation applications, the limited durability and reliability hinder their full commercialization. Assessing internal health states is critical to overcoming these challenges by preventing operational faults and minimizing degradation rates. However, hydrogen fuel cells are highly nonlinear, multiscale, and multiphysics systems, hindering the estimation of system health states. This review investigates a nondestructive and in situ characterization technique, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), to characterize the health states of hydrogen fuel cells. The variation in internal health states is directly reflected in the impedance spectrum, which can be assessed through proper interpretation. Nevertheless, developing EIS for hydrogen fuel cells is a nontrivial task. Implementing and applying EIS requires interdisciplinary studies in signal processing, control theory, and machine learning in some particular cases. This review systematically discusses EIS’s implementation, interpretation, and application for hydrogen fuel cells. The onboard applicability and short measuring time are key factors in EIS implementation. Model-based and model-free interpretation approaches are reviewed for efficiently extracting valuable health states. Based on these results, the application of EIS to performance characterization, fault diagnosis, degradation analysis, and prognostics is discussed. Four perspectives regarding general, non-electrical, localized, and multiphysics-integrated EIS, are proposed to highlight and guide the EIS-related studies in hydrogen fuel cells. This review offers comprehensive perspectives on the deployment and application of EIS in hydrogen fuel cells, providing valuable insights for academic researchers and industry practitioners in addressing the durability and reliability challenges.

title: Radical C─N Coupling at Electrified Carbon Nanotube Interfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrogen‐containing motifs are central to pharmaceuticals, materials, and bioactive molecules, yet controlling radical C─N bond formation under mild and catalyst‐free conditions remains challenging. Here, we report an electrified carbon nanotube (CNT) interface that promotes radical C─N coupling of aniline derivatives and N ‐containing heterocyclic compounds under ambient conditions. Mechanistic experiments show that the enhanced reactivity arises from the coupling of the applied electric field with interfacial charge transfer through the CNT network. Radical trapping, redox probing, and density functional theory calculations support a field‐assisted electron‐transfer pathway involving nitrogen‐centered radical intermediates. Our results indicate that the applied field lowers the barrier to radical generation, underscoring its critical role in enabling the reaction. This work demonstrates that conductive nanointerfaces can enable localized radical bond‐forming chemistry under an externally applied electric field.

title: Real‐Time Discrimination of Parallel Single‐Cell Exocytotic and Exosome Catecholamine Signaling by Multichannel Hollow Nanoelectrodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical communication in single cells often involves multiple vesicle release pathways that can carry overlapping messenger molecules. However, existing methods cannot discriminate between these pathways simultaneously under matched conditions, making their intrinsic relationship difficult to resolve. Here we establish a multichannel hollow carbon nanoelectrode‐based strategy for real‐time discrimination of classical exocytosis and exosome‐associated release. Distinct electrochemical signatures generated within the hollow geometry enable pathway resolution, while the multichannel architecture expands effective sampling coverage over the cell surface and improves event capture efficiency. Using this approach, we show that the two catecholamine signaling routes remain active under environmental perturbation but exhibit non‐compensatory changes in release activity. Under cargo‐loading disruption, classical exocytosis retains reduced catecholamine output, whereas exosome‐associated release persists but becomes largely chemically silent. These findings uncover a previously inaccessible chemically silent state of exosome‐associated release and reveal that cells can preserve a release pathway while selectively reshaping its chemical consequence. More broadly, this work shows that parallel release routes can convey fundamentally different chemical information under the same cellular conditions and establishes a general strategy for studying pathway‐specific chemical regulation in other secretory systems.

title: Each Atom and Electron Matters: A Continuous Gold Nanocluster Series
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving continuous atom‐by‐atom structural evolution and elucidating the associated quantum size effects in metal nanoclusters remain highly challenging, primarily due to the intrinsic thermodynamic preference for discrete magic‐number configurations. In this study, we present a synergistic ligand‐engineering strategy that combines dynamic ligand coordination with fluorine chemistry to break this preference. The use of weakly coordinating phosphine ligands facilitates adaptive ligand rearrangement during progressive core expansion, while fluorine‐induced noncovalent interactions establish a robust molecular and supramolecular spatial lock, thereby stabilizing cluster molecules and enhancing crystallization. Through this approach, we successfully isolated and structurally characterized an unprecedented continuous series of gold nanoclusters: Au 41 –Au 44 . Comprehensive experimental and computational structural and photophysical analyses reveal non‐monotonic geometric evolution and atom‐specific modulation of electronic structure, thereby providing direct evidence for the principle that “each atom and electron matters” in dictating cluster geometry and electronic structures. Collectively, this work fills the structural gap in medium‐sized, phosphine‐protected gold nanoclusters and provides a continuous cluster series that serves as an ideal model for probing quantum size effects at the atomic level.

title: Evolution‐Inspired Multi‐Objective Bayesian Optimization for Protein Engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT Protein engineering requires efficient navigation of vast sequence spaces under limited evaluation budgets, especially when multiple properties must be optimized simultaneously. We developed evolution‐inspired multi‐objective Bayesian optimization (EvoMOBO), an active‐learning framework that integrates path‐dependent sequence generation, global candidate competition, and explicit multi‐objective optimization, enabling efficient prioritization of high‐value variants without exhaustive library enumeration. Compared with state‐of‐the‐art methods on complete steroid receptor DNA‐binding domain (DBD) and ParD3 antitoxin landscapes, EvoMOBO achieved greater target‐region enrichment while maintaining sequence diversity across two‐ and three‐objective tasks. In the DBD landscape, optimization guided by simulation‐derived geometric descriptors enriched variants with satisfactory experimental performance without experimental labels. Building on this validation, we applied EvoMOBO to two enzyme‐engineering tasks using mechanistic descriptors, with experiments reserved for final validation. For an old yellow enzyme from Geobacillus kaustophilus , probabilities of substrate binding and reaction preorganization guided optimization of a non‐native oxidative dehydrogenation, yielding a variant that increased substrate conversion from 17.5% to 95%. For a formate oxidase from Aspergillus oryzae , stability‐related descriptors identified aggregation‐resistant variants that nearly doubled diethyl phthalate degradation in a photoenzymatic cascade. Together, these results demonstrate robust multi‐objective optimization by EvoMOBO and show that mechanism‐derived descriptors can effectively guide protein engineering toward experimentally improved functions.

title: Electrostatic Cation Intercalation Into Polymeric Self‐Assembled Monolayers Enables Ambient‐Air Fabrication of 32.73% Efficient Monolithic Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymeric self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) enable stable, efficient, and scalable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs) based on silicon heterojunction (HJT) bottom cells. However, severe steric hindrance within the polymer matrix disrupts the directional anchoring of phosphonate groups, thereby limiting macroscopic work‐function regulation and sustaining a persistent hole‐extraction barrier. Herein, we report a targeted molecular reconstruction of the buried interface via the electrostatic intercalation of phenethylammonium iodide (PEAI). Templated by the polymer backbone, the intercalated PEA + cations adopt a highly directional vertical arrangement. This oriented molecular scaffold provides a strong intrinsic dipole while driving the electronegative iodide (I − ) counterions to enrich at the uppermost interface. This synergistic spatial decoupling maximizes the net upward dipole, triggering a favorable energy level realignment that effectively overcomes the hole extraction barrier. Concurrently, the halide‐enriched SAM dictates crystallization kinetics during ambient‐air slot‐die coating, inducing rapid “burst nucleation” to minimize solvate intermediates and suppress basal voids. Consequently, our 1 cm 2 TSC achieves an independently certified power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 32.73%. Benefiting from monolithic crystallographic integrity, the unencapsulated device maintains an enhanced T 80 lifetime of 2182 h under continuous maximum power point tracking.

title: The Elusive Fluoropolysulfates [FS 2 O 6 ] – and [FS 3 O 9 ] – , a New Class of Weakly Coordinating Anions
abstract: ABSTRACT The isolation and structural characterization of the fluorodi‐ and fluorotrisulfate anions, [FS 2 O 6 ] – and [FS 3 O 9 ] – are reported. The [FS 2 O 6 ] – anion has been obtained from reactions of SO 3 with XeF 2 in the presence of PbF 2 as the salt Pb[FSO 3 ][FS 2 O 6 ] (triclinic, P , Z = 2, a = 508.65(3), b = 909.67(5), c = 969.67(5) pm, α = 89.494(2)°, β = 77.373(2)°, γ = 76.466(2)° and V = 424.99(4) Å 3 ). The [FS 3 O 9 ] – ion forms in the reaction of K[FSO 3 ] with SO 3 at room temperature as the potassium salt K[FS 3 O 9 ] (monoclinic, P 2 1 / c , Z = 4, a = 1048.69(8), b = 786.39(6), c = 969.58(7) pm, β = 90.431(2)° and V = 799.6(1) Å 3 ). The use of the [FS 3 O 9 ] – ion as a weakly coordinating anion was demonstrated with the isolation of [Se 4 ][FS 3 O 9 ] 2 (monoclinic, P 2 1 / n , Z = 2, a = 719.2(1), b = 1576.0(2), c = 897.7(1) pm, β = 113.015(5)° and V = 936.5(2) Å 3 ), obtained from the reaction of selenium, SO 3 and XeF 2 at 80°C. We investigated the anions quantum chemically concerning their molecular electrostatic potentials and the electronic energies of formation. The non–covalent interactions in [Se 4 ][FS 3 O 9 ] 2 were analysed using Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) and Natural Bond Orbital Analysis (NBO).

title: Spin‐Correlated Wavelength–Intensity Dual Modulation in Organic Diradicals via Excited‐State Channel Engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT Luminescent diradicals translate open‐shell spin dynamics into optical readouts, yet their spin‐dependent responses have largely been confined to emission‐intensity changes, while concurrent wavelength modulation remains rare. Here, we introduce a through‐space charge‐transfer (TSCT) strategy in which appending a δ‐carboline donor to a carbazole‐bridged diradical preserves the native through‐bond charge‐transfer (TBCT) pathway while introducing a higher‐energy TSCT‐related emissive channel. At low temperature, δCbCz(TTM) 2 exhibits pronounced magnetoluminescence (MagLum) enhancement together with an approximately 31 nm field‐induced blue shift, while zero‐field warming from 4.5 to 20 K produces an approximately 25 nm blue shift. Temperature‐dependent MagLum measurements show that the additional spectral and intensity changes induced by the magnetic field are rapidly attenuated upon warming, supporting a common spin‐dependent mechanism. The structural analogue αCbCz(TTM) 2 exhibits a similar dual response with a smaller wavelength shift, highlighting the sensitivity of the response to donor topology. Time‐resolved spectroscopy, variable‐temperature EPR, and quantum–chemical calculations support a spin‐correlated photophysical model in which magnetic and thermal perturbations regulate spin‐dependent population redistribution, thereby modulating the relative contributions of TBCT‐ and TSCT‐related emissive channels and producing correlated changes in emission intensity and wavelength. This work establishes through‐space excited‐state channel engineering as a route for extending spin‐correlated luminescence beyond intensity‐only modulation.

title: Distinct PXR Inverse Agonism Mechanisms Rely on Differential Ligand‐induced Co‐Regulator Recruitment
abstract: ABSTRACT The pregnane X receptor (PXR) displays exceptional ligand promiscuity, yet the molecular basis of its antagonism remains poorly defined. PXR inhibition has traditionally been attributed to the displacement of coactivators from the activation function‐2 (AF‐2) surface. Here, we show that PXR antagonism is mechanistically heterogeneous, with distinct inhibitory mechanisms determined by ligand structure. Comparative analysis of imidazo[1,2‐a]pyridine, MI891, and SPA70 antagonists reveals multiple non‐canonical inhibitory mechanisms that decouple coregulator recruitment from transcriptional output. Notably, SPA70 preserves compatibility with coactivator recruitment while remaining transcriptionally inactive, consistent with concurrent corepressor engagement and a distinct coactivator‐compatible antagonist state. In contrast, MI891 stabilizes a PXR conformation that favors NCoR1 and SMRT binding and impairs nuclear translocation. MD simulations and mutagenesis reveal ligand‐specific perturbations of α12 and the α10/α11 region that underlie these effects. Together, these findings establish a ligand‐encoded framework for PXR antagonism that extends beyond the classical on/off switch model.

title: A Single‐COF Photocatalytic System for One‐Pot Oxygen Reduction Coupled Ammoximation of Cyclic Ketones
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic oxygen reduction over covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has been extensively studied for H 2 O 2 production, but the in situ utilization of oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) intermediates in chemical synthesis remains underexplored. Herein, two porphyrin‐based polyimide COFs, IMCOF‐1 and IMCOF‐2, are reported as photocatalysts for the one‐pot ORR‐coupled ammoximation of cyclic ketones using O 2 and NH 4 OAc. Under light irradiation, IMCOF‐1 achieves a cyclohexanone oxime formation rate of 18.55 mmol g −1 h −1 and is effective for several other cyclic ketones. Mechanistic investigations reveal that photoinduced electron transfer from the porphyrin units to the electron‐deficient imide moieties promotes charge separation and activates O 2 at the carbonyl sites. The resulting surface‐bound *OOH intermediates are proposed to participate in ammonia oxidation and subsequent NH 2 OH formation, which then condenses with cyclic ketones to yield the corresponding oximes. In contrast to stepwise systems that first accumulate H 2 O 2 before ammoximation, the present one‐pot strategy enables the in situ utilization of oxygen‐derived reactive intermediates without requiring substantial bulk H 2 O 2 pre‐accumulation, eliminating the need for H 2 O 2 isolation, storage, and transport, thereby improving safety and atom economy while maintaining high selectivity. This work demonstrates the potential of directly harnessing ORR‐derived intermediates for the light‐driven synthesis of value‐added nitrogen‐containing chemicals.

title: Single‐Step Orientational Self‐Assembly of Pd Metallacycles and Heterometallic Pd–Pt Helical Cages From Heteroditopic Ligands
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling the self‐assembly of heterometallic supramolecular architectures without generating statistical mixtures remains a major challenge. Here, we show that adaptable coordination modes of tetrazole units in heterodipotic tetrazole–pyridine ligands direct both orientational self‐sorting and selective metal organization. Reaction with cis‐protected Pd(II) acceptors afforded Pd 6 ( L ) 4 metallacycles ( L = L1 – L3 ), in which tetrazolate coordination through an unusual (2,3) binding mode is exploited in the orientational self‐sorting. In contrast, ligand L4 employed its (1,3) coordination mode together with the pyridyl donors to generate a Pd 9 ( L4 ) 6 helical cage and the heterometallic Pd 9 Ag( L4 ) 6 , and Pd 3 Pt 6 ( L4 ) 6 cages in single‐step self‐assembly processes. Remarkably, despite the closely matched coordination preferences of Pd(II) and Pt(II), the synergistic effects of donor inequivalence and the flexible coordination behavior selectively partitions the two congeneric d 8 ions into distinct coordination sites within the Pd 3 Pt 6 ( L4 ) 6 cage. The uncommon (1,2,3) tetrazolate binding mode additionally enables formation of the Pd 9 Ag( L4 ) 6 cage. Encapsulation of enantiopure guests by the helical cages induces host chirality and corresponding chiroptical responses. These results demonstrate that coordination mode flexibility of the tetrazole moiety combined with the pyridyl unit can direct the formation of metallacycles and helical cages and enable selective partitioning of closely related metal ions in a single‐step assembly.

title: A Homoleptic Biradicaloid‐Ligated Analogue of Ferrocene
abstract: ABSTRACT In this communication, we report the synthesis, characterisation and electronic structure of a ferrocene analogue containing two biradicaloid ligands, representing the first homoleptic sandwich complex in this ligand class. In this quest, we found that the target compound was unattainable via routes involving Fe(0) or Fe(II) intermediates, and counterintuitively that the rare and much less‐explored +1 oxidation state was crucial for the synthesis.

title: Addition–Migration Cascade for Ortho ‐Selective Carbon Functionalization of Phenols
abstract: ABSTRACT Ortho ‐ and para ‐carbon‐disubstituted phenols are prevalent in natural products and pharmaceuticals, yet their selective synthesis remains challenging. The strong resonance‐donating effect of the hydroxyl group renders phenols electron‐rich, activates both ortho and para positions, and limits their direct functionalization with external nucleophiles. Herein, we report an addition–migration–rearomatization strategy for the ortho ‐selective carbon functionalization of phenols using readily accessible para ‐quinol carbonates and diverse organometallic nucleophiles. The transformation proceeds through nucleophilic 1,2‐addition to the dienone carbonyl, followed by C1‐to‐C2 group migration and rearomatization, thereby enabling the formal installation of carbon nucleophilic substituents at the enone α‐position. A broad range of sp 3 ‐, sp 2 ‐, and sp ‐hybridized nucleophiles, including alkyl, vinyl, aryl, heteroaryl, polyaromatic, and alkynyl reagents, participate efficiently under mild conditions. DFT calculations identify syn ‐methyl facial attack as kinetically preferred over syn ‐Boc facial attack by 24.72 kcal mol − 1 , establish that both S N 2′ manifolds are noncompetitive, and show that aromatization proceeds via a Mg‐assisted decarboxylation/deprotonation pathway rather than an unassisted route. Synthetic utility is demonstrated through a concise five step synthesis of the bioactive natural product honokiol from commercially available allyl anisole.

title: Nanoimprint lithography for metasurfaces built from functional nanoparticles
abstract: Combining nanoimprint lithography with functional nanoparticles brings two design levers into the same platform: the geometry of a metasurface and the optical properties of its material. This review shows how these two levels of control are combined across the metallic, dielectric, light-emitting, and hybrid systems, providing a scalable framework for flat optics with tunable and multifunctional responses.

Robotic inspection and maintenance for energy infrastructure: a systematic review and future perspectives
Empirical validation of a dual-defense mechanism reshaping wholesale electricity price dynamics in Singapore
Advances in sorption-based thermochemical energy storage: from material properties to prototype-level performance

Frequency-constrained robust unit commitment for an integrated electricity-heat system considering heterogeneous resources
Data center cooling in the AI era: cross-scale challenges and system-level outlook
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping data center thermal and energy requirements, driven by increasing power densities and heterogeneous workload characteristics. This review provides an integrated cross-scale and temporal perspective that connects AI heat generation with chip-, rack-, and facility-scale thermal management and their interactions with external energy, water, and grid infrastructures. Modern AI workloads, enabled by accelerator-based hardware, can generate highly localized and temporally dynamic heat fluxes, challenging traditional assumptions of uniform and steady-state cooling design. Accordingly, a range of cooling technologies is examined, including air-based systems, liquid cooling approaches, hybrid configurations, and heat-reuse strategies, with emphasis on their performance limits and deployment constraints. The analysis further identifies key cross-cutting barriers to scalability and efficiency, including thermodynamic irreversibility, coupled water–energy–grid dependencies, cross-scale thermal interactions, reliability and maintainability constraints, and technology-specific trade-offs. Building on these observations, future cooling systems are expected to shift toward integrated and adaptive designs that prioritize multi-objective optimization rather than isolated performance improvements. Emerging directions include grid-responsive and water-aware operation, thermal storage-enabled temporal decoupling, co-designed computing and cooling infrastructures, and predictive closed-loop thermal management enabled by digital twins and data-driven control. Collectively, the findings highlight a transition from component-level optimization toward fully integrated system architectures that jointly optimize energy efficiency, resource utilization, operational resilience, and computational performance across spatial and temporal scales.

title: Tunable molecular selectivity in CO2 conversion via exsolution-engineered catalytic interfaces
abstract: Turning CO2 into useful hydrocarbons usually means broad product mixtures and high-pressure reactors since conventional catalysts offer little control over chain length and require high pressures to form C–C bonds. Here, we provide a generalizable route to C–C selectivity control through the formation of distinct catalytic interfaces via exsolution engineering. Hence, product choice is set by parent material design rather than reaction condition requirements. Beyond performance, this establishes a design strategy connecting interface structure to product selectivity.

title: Absolute quantification and profiling of cellular tRNAs by nanopore sequencing and a deep learning classifier
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Transfer RNAs (tRNAs) link mRNA codons to amino acids during translation. Their abundance and modification states are dynamically regulated and influence translation efficiency, mRNA stability, and proteostasis. Accurate profiling of tRNAs is essential, but deep sequencing suffers from modification-induced biases during cDNA synthesis, while nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) still faces challenges in accurate tRNA profiling. Here, we develop an end-to-end deep learning model, termed nano tRNA classifier, that directly uses nanopore-DRS ionic current signals to classify tRNAs without basecalling. The model achieves 98.2% classification accuracy with high read retention across all Escherichia coli tRNA species. Using an equimolar mixture of native tRNAs as a ground-truth reference, we correct read-count bias, enabling absolute quantification and profiling under diverse culture conditions. We further develop binary classifiers that detect specific tRNA modifications at the single-molecule level with high accuracy. This nanopore-based platform integrates accurate tRNA classification, absolute quantification, and single-molecule modification detection.

title: Calpain-mediated TBP cleavage disturbs neuronal AMOT-YAP1 signalling
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The transcription factor TATA-box-binding protein (TBP) plays a crucial role in neurons, as highlighted by its involvement in spinocerebellar ataxia type 17 (SCA17), where pathological polyglutamine expansions disrupt its function. While the molecular pathomechanisms remain unclear, our previous study showed that calcium-activated calpains cleave TBP in SCA17 cell and animal models. Here, we pinpoint a major calpain cleavage site after residue T106, C-terminal to TBP’s polyglutamine tract. The resulting polyglutamine-containing N-terminal fragments mislocalise to the cytoplasm and exhibit increased aggregation. Both the N-terminal and the nuclear-localised C-terminal fragments contribute to calpain overactivation. SCA17 cell line-based multi-omics analyses revealed that TBP fragments alter pathways linked to neuronal function and neurodegeneration, identifying AMOT as a key player. Further analyses in SCA17 cell lines, patient-derived fibroblasts and induced neurons as well as in rat and zebrafish models confirmed AMOT’s pivotal role in neurons, regulated by TBP and mediated via YAP1-dependent signalling. These findings offer further insights into TBP’s neuronal function and suggest broader implications of AMOT for neurodegenerative and neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: Electrostatic Presolvation Enables Selectivity in Photoinduced Ligand Exchange
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Functional group compatibility remains a central challenge in photochemical C–H activation with metal complexes. Strongly donating groups preferentially coordinate to the reactive unsaturated metal and suppress weaker C–H coordination and σ-complex formation required for C–H bond activation. Controlling the initial coordination in photoinduced ligand exchange is therefore one approach to achieving selectivity in bond activation. Here, we resolve the elementary steps of photoinduced CO to acetonitrile ligand substitution for Rh(acac)(CO)2 with femtosecond-resolution X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the Rh L3-edge. We directly observe the formation of a hitherto undetected transient acetonitrile C–H σ-complex and its subsequent rearrangement to the thermodynamically favored nitrogen-coordinated solvent complex. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the initial C–H coordination is enabled by electrostatic presolvation, which orients the acetonitrile methyl groups toward the metal center prior to CO dissociation. Our results point to a general strategy to direct selectivity in C–H activation by controlling coordination through presolvation.

title: Maximizing the Photocatalytic Performance of Covalent Organic Frameworks by Decoupling Charge Separation and Recombination via Guest π-Conjugation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising candidates for solar-driven photocatalysis; however, simultaneously achieving ultrafast electron–hole separation and suppressed charge recombination remains challenging. Here, we demonstrated a theory-guided design of high-performance host–guest COFs by tuning π-conjugation of embedded guest molecules. Combining many-body nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations based on linear response time-dependent density functional theory with transient spectroscopy and photocatalytic experiments, we elucidate the microscopic mechanisms governing excited-state dynamics in these systems. Our simulations suggest that increasing guest π-conjugation enables subpicosecond hole transfer from the COF host to the guest molecules by lowering the acceptor excitation energy and enhancing the density of acceptor states. Simultaneously, charge recombination is strongly suppressed through two synergistic effects. First, highly π-conjugated guests enhance low-frequency structural fluctuations and excited-state energetic disorder, thereby accelerating quantum decoherence. Second, increased guest π-conjugation promotes spatial separation of electrons and holes, while stronger instantaneous structural fluctuations under ambient conditions further localize charge carriers. These effects reduce electron–hole overlap and nonadiabatic coupling and markedly slow recombination relative to less conjugated systems. Femtosecond pump–probe spectroscopy supports the predicted guest-dependent differences in early excited-state dynamics. Guided by these mechanistic insights, we demonstrate experimentally that COFs incorporating highly conjugated guest molecules exhibit superior photocatalytic performance, achieving up to 97.38% conversion of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural with excellent product selectivity. The work establishes a molecular-level understanding of how guest properties govern excited-state dynamics in host–guest COFs and provides general design principles for developing high-performance photocatalysts.

title: Monomer Flexibility Enables the Regulation of Interlayer Stacking in Two-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Precise control over interlayer stacking in two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) remains far less developed than the design of in-plane topology. Here, rather than regulating stacking through external changes in the crystallization medium, we investigate the conformational compatibility of paired monomers as an internal molecular variable for directing the out-of-plane organization of 2D COFs. A topologically related series of eight imine-linked COFs was constructed using different combinations of flexible and rigid monomers. Within the present COF series, flexible-flexible monomer combinations were associated with AA′ stacking, whereas flexible-rigid combinations were associated with ABC stacking. These distinct stacking outcomes are associated with different conformational responses during framework formation. The resulting stacking-defined pore environments further give rise to different xylene adsorption and separation behaviors, with the AA′-stacked COFs showing enhanced discrimination among xylene isomers. This work identifies monomer flexibility matching as an important molecular design consideration for regulating interlayer stacking, extending 2D COF design from in-plane topology to out-of-plane structural control.

title: Hydration water drives elastin’s entropic elasticity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Elastin endows arteries, skin and lungs with elasticity, yet the molecular origin of its entropic recoil remains debated. Using multi-microsecond all-atom simulations of a representative elastomeric region of human tropoelastin, the monomeric precursor of elastin, we quantify protein conformational entropy, hydration-water entropy, and protein- and water-mediated interaction enthalpies during stretching. Protein conformational entropy decreases modestly overall, with heterogeneous local entropic responses governed by secondary structure and sequence context. In contrast, hydration water provides the dominant unfavorable entropic contribution because stretching recruits many water molecules from bulk into a persistently low-entropy first hydration layer. Stretching also disrupts favorable intra-protein interactions while strengthening protein–water interactions, producing opposing enthalpic contributions that largely compensate the entropic penalty. Together, these results support a hydration-coupled thermodynamic mechanism in which water is the dominant entropic contributor to elastin recoil within a strongly compensating enthalpy–entropy balance.

title: X-Shaped Multichannel Conjugation Enabled by Excited-State Aromaticity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molecular topology governs the photophysical properties of polycyclic π-conjugated systems by defining their effective conjugation pathways. Conventionally, linear π-extension is considered more effective than angular extension in increasing the effective conjugation length and narrowing the optical bandgap. Here we uncover an inverse topology–property relationship in π-extended dihydrophenazines (DHPs): linear extension unexpectedly blueshifts fluorescence, whereas angular extension produces pronounced redshifts. Transient spectroscopy, theoretical calculations and aromaticity analyses reveal that Baird aromaticity–driven planarization of the DHP core redistributes π-delocalization in the S1 state, causing linear fusion to disrupt global π-delocalization and shorten the effective conjugation length, while angular fusion promotes cooperative delocalization across the fused framework and extends it. Successive angular fusion progressively activates four structurally distinct π-extension branches through the shared Baird-aromatic DHP core, generating an X-shaped multichannel conjugation network. These findings reveal how excited-state aromaticity reprograms conjugation topology, offering new insights for controlling π-delocalization and emission.

title: Molecular Origins of Solvent Effects in Cyclohexanol Dehydration on H-BEA Zeolite
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Solvents can substantially alter reaction rates by modifying the thermodynamic states of substrates and the free-energy landscapes of elementary steps in acid-catalyzed reactions. Cyclohexanol dehydration within BEA-type zeolite was investigated experimentally and theoretically to elucidate solvent effects on elementary steps. Adsorbed alcohol monomers and dimers were identified in acetone, cyclohexanol, 1,4-dioxane, methanol, and decalin. Hydrated hydronium ions formed in water at Brønsted acid sites (BAS), while solvents interact with protonated cyclohexanol. Kinetic H/D isotope effects (KIE) revealed solvent-dependent rate-determining steps of C–O cleavage (KIE < 2) in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and decalin, while C–H cleavage (KIE > 2) dominates in water and methanol. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations showed that acetone induces dissociation of protonated cyclohexanol from BAS to form solvated cyclohexanol-acetone complexes, whereas 1,4-dioxane and decalin leave the alcohol bound to the framework, providing a molecular-level rationale for higher dehydration rates in acetone. Solvation in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and methanol destabilizes the initial state (excess chemical potential) by 11–13 kJ/mol, compared to 6–7 kJ/mol in water and decalin. The excess chemical potential of the transition state correlates well with the free-energy barrier of the rate-determining step. The excess chemical potential of C–O cleavage transition states in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and decalin shows greater stabilization (−21 to −11 kJ/mol) than C–H cleavage in water and methanol (−5 to −1 kJ/mol). The combined initial-state and transition-state (de)stabilization yields reaction rates up to 3 orders of magnitude higher in acetone compared to water and decalin.

title: Nanometer-resolution imaging of living bacteria across species and cellular orientations
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The bacterial cell envelope is a complex superstructure that is an important target and a major barrier for antibiotics. To date, highest-resolution images of native cell envelopes have been obtained by atomic force microscopy (AFM), but its use is limited by challenges in bacterial immobilization. We establish glutaraldehyde-functionalized glass surfaces for reversible covalent attachment, enabling robust adhesion across species and cellular orientations while preserving cell viability and growth. This approach allowed imaging of Escherichia coli both expressing O-antigen and fully lacking lipopolysaccharide (LPS) oligosaccharides, revealing that AFM contrast depends on LPS complexity and confirming previously observed outer membrane domains as LPS-enriched islands. It also enabled imaging of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii outer membranes, which lack the characteristic protein trimers observed in model E. coli. Finally, we discovered growth-phase dependent alterations in E. coli pole morphology, where trimer networks typical of exponential-phase cells were unresolved and morphological defects appeared.

title: Cationic Ionomer Coatings Promote Anion Electroreduction: Nitrate Reduction as a Model Reaction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrolysis technologies represent a promising pathway to valorize abundant feedstocks using renewable electricity. While ionomers serve critical roles as ion conductors and catalyst binders in electrolyzers, their impact on electrochemical transformations of ionic species remains poorly understood compared to extensively studied neutral-molecule conversions like water splitting and CO2 reduction. Herein, we use the electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction as a model transformation to investigate the influence of ionomer coatings in anion electroreduction reactions, which face fundamental challenges from electrostatic anion depletion near negatively polarized cathodes and premature desorption of anionic intermediates. We demonstrate that cationic ionomer coatings increase local nitrate concentration up to 10-fold compared to bulk electrolyte due to the interfacial Donnan potential. While prior studies have shown that ionomers can influence the local reaction microenvironment, this work provides, to the best of our knowledge, the first quantitative measurement of nitrate concentration within ionomer coatings as a function of charge density and its impact on catalysis. A 5-fold enhancement in ammonium partial current density was achieved with the ionomer bearing the highest charge density. Using in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS), we quantified enhanced local nitrate concentration (up to 1.1 M versus 0.1 M in bulk electrolyte), conversion, and supply with increasing charge density. This study establishes guiding principles for tuning ionomer charge identity and density to control interfacial ion concentrations in electrochemical transformations of dilute charged substrates.

title: An Embedded Plasticization Strategy for Flexible Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Polymers with High Luminance
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) polymers offer the theoretical advantage of achieving 100% internal quantum efficiency. Together with their solution processability, TADF polymers are promising candidates for flexible display technologies. However, emissive polymers that simultaneously combine efficient TADF emission with mechanical flexibility remain rare. Here, we report an embedded plasticized linker strategy for mechanically compliant TADF polymers. Polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based flexible segments are covalently incorporated into acridine–benzophenone–carbazole polymer backbones. This “TADF unit + plasticized linker” design preserves the donor–acceptor electronic structure required for delayed fluorescence while introducing flexibility into the emissive polymer framework. The resulting polymers exhibit small singlet–triplet energy gaps, clear delayed fluorescence, and favorable film deformability. The deformation behavior of the neat polymer films was evaluated on PDMS substrates under an applied substrate strain of 75%. Notably, the optimized rigid organic light-emitting diode (OLED) based on PIDC(2,7)-EO achieves a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 20.1% and a high luminance of 85 988 cd m–2. This luminance value is among the highest reported for polymer-based TADF OLEDs. Flexible OLEDs fabricated on flexible substrates further deliver a maximum EQE of 14.7%. These results demonstrate efficient electroluminescence from flexible device architectures. This work establishes embedded plasticized linkers as an effective molecular design strategy for high-performance mechanically flexible TADF polymers. This strategy provides a promising route toward next-generation flexible OLED technologies.

title: A Mixed Conducting Polymer with pH-Dependent Selectivity for the Oxygen Reduction Reaction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving 4-electron oxygen reduction with metal-free electrodes has remained a longstanding challenge. Here, we show that poly(benzimidazobenzophenanthroline) (BBL), an n-type ladder polymer, breaks this barrier through an electrocatalytic inner-sphere 2 + 2 series mechanism─a mode of reactivity unprecedented among organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs). Using pH-dependent rotating ring-disk voltammetry, we find that this series mechanism occurs over separate potential windows on BBL. At more positive potentials, an initial reduction wave correlated with electron polaron formation in BBL produces exclusively hydro(gen) peroxide across all pH values, followed by a second, pH-dependent wave for hydro(gen) peroxide reduction at more negative potentials. At pH 14.0, this second wave enables complete four-electron reduction of O2 (n ≈ 4) to OH–, driven by formation of a bipolaronic state in BBL. Decreasing the pH instead stabilizes a hydrogenated state in BBL incapable of O–O bond cleavage, reverting selectivity to n ≈ 2. These insights reveal that the coupling between ion selectivity during electrochemical ion-insertion and product selectivity during ORR catalysis shapes active-site structure and poisoning, establishing a new design principle in the emerging field of OMIEC electrocatalysis.

title: Interfacial Electric Field Dynamically Confined Enzyme Self-Adaptation in Covalent Organic Framework Heterojunctions for Photoenzymatic Catalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Artificial photoenzymatic synthesis systems based on 1,4-NADH-dependent enzymes are challenged by unclear interfacial interactions and limited stability. Inspired by the ordered assembly and Z-scheme electron transfer mechanism in natural photosynthesis, we constructed an enzyme self-adaptive covalent organic frameworks (COFs) immobilization platform featuring a built-in electric field and a targeted Z-scheme electron transfer pathway. The CT-COF@Py-COF served as a mechanical scaffold for in situ encapsulation of reductases at the heterojunction interface, where electrostatic interactions, π–π stacking, and the ensuing formation of an interfacial electric field (IEF) collectively facilitated enzyme encapsulation. Moreover, IEF drove the conformational self-adaptation of encapsulated reductases and promoted directional charge transfer across the Z-scheme heterojunction, which synergistically enhanced catalytic activity and operational stability. The IEF-integrated system, paired with various dehydrogenases, enabled the efficient synthesis of pharmaceutical precursors under visible light. In a continuous-flow reactor, the encapsulated dehydrogenase retained approximately 88% of its initial-cycle glycine-production activity after eight cycles and exhibited a 7.18-fold increase in lactate yield when coupled with light-driven 1,4-NADH regeneration. This study provides a platform that utilizes IEF to dynamically confine enzymes’ self-adaptation in COF heterojunctions for photoenzymatic synthesis of high-value products.

title: Techno-economic optimization of a low-carbon ammonia synthesis system integrated with coal-to‑hydrogen and power-to‑hydrogen production
Two functionally distinct amyloid-β intermediates link aggregation pathways to pathology in Alzheimer’s disease
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Neurotoxic intermediates formed during amyloid-β (Aβ) aggregation are thought to drive Alzheimer’s disease, yet their rarity and transient nature have obscured their identity and formation pathways in the human brain. Here, we combine super-resolution microscopy and single-molecule functional imaging with kinetic modelling to classify Aβ intermediates according to their membrane-disrupting activity and connect their damaging effects to the aggregation pathways that generate them. Applying this framework to recombinant Aβ42, an Alzheimer’s knock-in mouse model and human Alzheimer’s brain tissue, we find two functionally distinct intermediate populations present across all systems. They form through separate aggregation routes and differ in their neurotoxicity, abundance and susceptibility to inhibition. Both damage neurons and glia, but only one converts into plaques. Suppressing these intermediates pharmacologically in mice reduces plaque burden, attenuates astrogliosis and improves cognition. Our findings connect model systems with human pathology and identify intermediate formation pathways as actionable therapeutic targets across protein-misfolding disorders.

title: Electrode-associated growth reveals structure of OmcZ-type cytochrome nanowires in anaerobic methanotrophic archaea
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Anaerobic methanotrophic (ANME) archaea are key regulators of methane emissions in anoxic environments, yet their physiology remains poorly understood due to the lack of axenic cultures. Here, we show that cultivation on poised electrodes yields near-axenic cultures (95.8% relative abundance) of a freshwater ANME, for which we propose the name ‘Candidatus Methanoperedens vercellensis’. We identified key physiological properties of ‘Ca. M. vercellensis’: doubling times of 4.6 days at 30 °C, menaquinone as respiratory electron carrier, the inability to oxidize ethane, and preferential reduction of iron oxides over nitrate after cultivation on electrodes. A 3.3 Å cryo-electron microscopy structure of filaments displayed on the archaeal surface revealed polymerized OmcZ-type cytochrome nanowires, which are homologous to OmcZ nanowires essential for long-range (>10 μm) extracellular electron transfer (EET) in Geobacter sulfurreducens. The archaeal OmcZ-type nanowires include dense, collinear stacking of protected hemesakin to bacterial OmcZ nanowires, but with post-translational modification, thus yielding morphology distinct from bacterial OmcZ nanowires. Notably, in contrast to bacterial OmcZ, archaeal OmcZ-type nanowires do not form interconnected networks, and hemes are less solvent-exposed, which can protect them from the environment. Surprisingly, these archaea assemble OmcZ into nanowires even in the apparent absence of prolyl isomerase involved in folding bacterial OmcZ. This work establishes a model system for molecular understanding of nanowire-mediated EET in archaea.

title: Confocal-Detection Electrochemiluminescence Microscopy for Three-Dimensional Imaging of Electrochemical Reaction Fields
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemiluminescence (ECL) imaging is an important tool for visualizing electrochemical reactions and is generally performed by wide-field microscopy, which efficiently collects weak emission. The price of this high photon-collection efficiency, however, is that axial information is collapsed into a depth-integrated projection, preventing three-dimensional (3D) visualization. Confocal detection is attractive for 3D ECL imaging because it can distinguish emission from different focal planes, yet its application to ECL has not been systematically explored, mainly because of the limited photon output of ECL reactions. Here, we construct a confocal-detection ECL (CD-ECL) microscopy platform and identify three factors that make CD-ECL difficult: the low efficiency of ECL reactions, which limits photon generation; the optical trade-off between photon collection and spatiotemporal resolution; and the intrinsic instability of ECL reactions, which causes the emission intensity to change during confocal scanning. To address these problems, we first built a shared-objective configuration to compare confocal and wide-field ECL detection. We then optimized the ECL reaction conditions to increase photon generation, examined the trade-off between photon number and spatiotemporal resolution, and developed cyclic volumetric acquisition (CVA) to reduce the influence of temporal intensity variations. Under the optimized conditions, CD-ECL produced 3D images of emission around graphite-felt electrodes and followed the time-dependent evolution of the ECL reaction field. These results establish a confocal optical-detection route to 3D ECL imaging and provide a proof-of-concept basis for depth-dependent and time-resolved measurements under photon-limited conditions.

title: Plant responses to blue light absorbing agrivoltaic systems
Accelerating wind-farm AEP evaluation by exploiting near-low-rank wake structure
Climate-driven screening maps and design rules for PCM-assisted cooling of photovoltaic modules
Social acceptance of a green ammonia hub in a remote coastal community – the case of Ísafjörður in Iceland
abstract: The International Maritime Organisation targets net-zero greenhouse gas emissions from international shipping by 2050, considering green ammonia to be a promising fuel for decarbonisation. However, development and deployment of this fuel is contingent not only on aspects such as techno-economic feasibility and supportive policy frameworks, but also on social acceptance (SA). This study examines the community-level SA of a potential green ammonia hub for maritime uses in Ísafjörður, Iceland, a remote coastal settlement with a strong maritime history. Based on sixteen semi-structured interviews with local stakeholders, the study identifies the key drivers and barriers influencing SA. It reveals that perceived benefits such as job creation and environmental protection function as drivers, while barriers stem from perceived concerns regarding safety, cost, and lack of clear governance. Guided by a community-adapted corporate sustainability classification and a PESTLE lens, identified themes are mapped across political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental dimensions. The findings indicate that political and governance conditions function as an important enabling condition for SA, particularly through the perceived need for clear legislative frameworks and government incentives. Rather than operating independently, these political conditions were closely intertwined with economic and technological considerations, influencing investment risk, infrastructure development, affordability, safety, and equitable benefit distribution. The study concludes that for a just maritime energy transition to succeed, national policymakers must prioritise the implementation of robust incentive mechanisms and strategic roadmaps that satisfactorily address local socio-economic realities and contexts.

title: Do international critical mineral prices influence energy access? Evidence from developing countries
Harnessing wind energy for rural development: the state-orchestrated approach to realizing community energy in rural China
Repeated loss of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet’s Amundsen Sea sector during late Pleistocene interglacials
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sea-level reconstructions and numerical models suggest that the vulnerable West Antarctic Ice Sheet underwent major mass losses during the late Pleistocene, raising global sea level by several metres. However, direct evidence from ice-sheet proximal records for such retreat has remained inconclusive. Here we investigate variations in clay mineral assemblages and past ocean temperatures archived in West Antarctic continental margin sediments during the last 800,000 years. Our results demonstrate that the supply of glacigenic detritus sourced from the main outlet glaciers in the Amundsen Sea sector of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet ceased almost entirely during all previous warm periods, documenting the loss of their drainage basins. Concomitant seawater warming, revealed by a microfossil proxy, is attributed to intensified deep-water advection towards Antarctica’s Pacific margin, which is corroborated by the clay mineralogical evidence. Our findings show that ocean forcing can drive major deglaciation of West Antarctica and related global sea-level rise.

title: Archival and palaeoenvironmental documentation of extreme climate events reveals generational amnesia in collective memory
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Collective memory shapes how societies respond to extreme climate events, yet long-term evidence on how the collective memory of such events becomes perceptually biased over time is lacking. Here, we utilise four centuries (1470–1900) of climatic archives from northern China, along with tree–ring–based hydroclimate reconstructions, which are validated against instrumental observations of Wet/Dry Index (1901–2000) to fill the gap. We find that historical records reveal systematic, non-random mismatches, where severity assessments are often biased toward recent experience rather than absolute climatic anomalies. Correlations between historical and natural records increase when the natural series is re-standardised using 20–40-year sliding windows, reflecting a generational offset. A heuristic agent-based model reproduces this pattern, suggesting that generational amnesia is sufficient to explain the offsets in perception of environmental change. We argue that historical archives carry a generational imprint of perceptual bias, in which the severity of climate extremes is judged against recent lived experience rather than long-term climate variability. This has implications for bias-aware corrections for risk assessment, adaptation, and paleoclimate reconstruction.

title: Crystal records of erupted vs. trapped magma in volcanic arcs
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Arc andesites are hybrids generated by mixing of mafic and silicic magmas. The silicic endmember can contribute to crustal growth or trigger explosive eruptions, yet remains difficult to constrain due to limited representation in the erupted record. Here, we show that textural, elemental and isotopic records preserved in plagioclase can distinguish between trapped and erupted crystal mush, thus constraining conditions of magma storage vs. eruption in arc systems. We define the plagioclase eruptibility field, a narrow and recurrent anorthite range (An~61) that represents erupted melt across Central Andes volcanoes upon mafic recharge. The recycled plagioclase cargo is dominantly An~43, recording prolonged crystallisation and assimilation within silicic mushes. This pattern repeats in continental and composite arcs globally, indicating strong eruptive filtering of arc magmas and widespread occurrence of dormant felsic and mafic mushes that, in most cases, contribute to crustal growth; yet exceptionally, felsic mushes can rapidly remobilise to generate super-eruptions.

title: The transcriptional regulator IκBζ is essential for ILC2 effector functions
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2) are the sentinels that ensure tissue homeostasis and engage in the immune response to helminths by secreting type 2 cytokines. Here we show that IκBζ, an atypical member of the IκB family, controls basal IL-5 production by ILC2s and governs their effector program during helminth infection and asthma. Peripheral ILC2s express IκBζ at steady state, and its expression is further induced upon stimulation with IL-33 or IL-25 in an NF-κB- and STAT3/5-dependent manner. Upon activation, IκBζ refines chromatin accessibility at regulatory elements of effector cytokine loci, thereby licensing transcription. Due to reduced type 2 cytokine secretion and impaired proliferative capacity of ILC2s, mice with IκBζ-deficient ILC2s show delayed clearance of the hookworm Nippostrongylus brasiliensis and reduced papain-induced airway inflammation. Taken together, our study highlights the central role of IκBζ in orchestrating the ILC2 effector program in different tissues in health and disease.

title: LLM ensemble PREVIA predicts future PTSD risk from emergency department trauma narratives with expert-level accuracy
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder affects numerous trauma survivors following emergency department discharge, making this encounter vital for early risk stratification. Yet emergency clinicians face severe time constraints, making existing screening tools impractical. We introduce PREVIA, a clinically-informed large language model ensemble, that predicts post-traumatic stress disorder risk from unstructured patient trauma narratives, collected in response to a routine-care question asked in the emergency department, by extracting early post-traumatic stress symptoms, peri-traumatic symptoms, risk, and protective factors. Within an ongoing longitudinal study, we included N = 145 patients across two New York City level-1 trauma centers within 24 hours of trauma and assessed post-traumatic stress disorder 1-month post-trauma. In this work, PREVIA accurately forecasts post-traumatic stress disorder (AUROC = 78.49% ± 5.75%, sensitivity=95.4% ± 3.99%, precision=46.76% ± 8.66%), performs comparably to an emergency clinician specialized in post-traumatic stress disorder on 30 randomly selected patients (PREVIA: AUROC = 84.39%, sensitivity=100.00%, precision=50.00%; clinician: AUROC = 83.86%, sensitivity=88.89%, precision=50.00%), and generates interpretable explanations without additional clinical burden. These initial findings support PREVIA’s potential as a scalable emergency department screener for timely, targeted interventions, and warrant validation in larger, independent cohorts.

title: Comment on “Self-organizing neuromorphic nanowire networks as stochastic dynamical systems"
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
