title: A replaceable soma enables negative senescence in harvester ants
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Most vertebrates and insects undergo senescence: as they age, their rate of mortality increases while reproduction declines. We present data from a 34-y study on 3,285 colonies of known age in the western harvester ant,
                    Pogonomyrmex occidentalis,
                    that show the reverse pattern, negative senescence, in which mortality decreases and reproduction increases with age. Theoretical models have identified indeterminate growth and a lack of reproductive cost to growth as the key traits favoring the evolution of negative senescence. Ant colonies continue to grow throughout their lifetime, leading to older colonies being larger on average. We found no evidence of a tradeoff between colony growth and reproduction: growth and reproduction were positively correlated, a synergism that may favor continued investment in growth. Harvester ants occupy a temporally variable environment that shapes investment in reproduction. At the population level, greater reproduction in 1 y does not lead to higher numbers of new colonies in the following year. Environmental unpredictability decouples reproduction from recruitment and selects for an extended reproductive lifespan, a trait that parallels changes in aging. We discuss the features that harvester ant colonies share with other organisms to identify functionally homologous mechanisms for avoiding senescence, as well as those traits that are specific to highly eusocial species.

title: The decision to stop “counting” explains numerical underproduction in primates
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Sequential numerical production requires generating a target number of actions, but the mechanisms governing the termination of counting sequences are unclear. We trained two rhesus macaques to produce instructed numerosities by generating the corresponding number of actions in response to sign numerals or dot arrays. Although action sequences were controlled for temporal parameters, both monkeys performed accurately across both stimulus formats. However, their performance accuracy showed a systematic asymmetry: underproduction occurred more often than overproduction, contrary to predictions from perceptual numerosity judgments governed by Weber–Fechner scaling. This asymmetry was mirrored in reaction times, with longer latencies for underproduced sequences and shorter latencies for overproduced ones. A stochastic accumulation-to-bound model in which a decision variable evolves across counting steps and triggers termination when a threshold is reached can account for both accuracy and reaction-time patterns. These results provide evidence for a sequential stopping process that contributes to numerical production, relating counting behavior to general principles of decision formation.

title: Targeting of STEAP3 by a selenium D–π–A photosensitizer that activates ferroptosis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Resistance to apoptosis limits the efficacy of many cancer therapies. Photodynamic therapy (PDT), with its spatial precision, offers a promising strategy by engaging nonapoptotic cell death pathways, such as ferroptosis. However, the direct molecular targets of most photosensitizers remain undefined. Here, we introduce a class of selenium-containing D–π–A photosensitizers (PDSe-1 to PDSe-11) and identify PDSe-8 as a lead system with advantageous photophysical properties and potent, hypoxia-tolerant phototoxicity (IC
                    50
                    = 53 nM). PDSe-8 elicits a concentration-dependent switching of cell death programs. Low doses trigger apoptosis through p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling, whereas higher doses activate ferroptosis. Competitive chemoproteomics reveals the metalloreductase STEAP3 as a direct molecular target of light-activated PDSe-8 underlying this switch. Upon photoirradiation, PDSe-8 photodegrades STEAP3 in glioblastoma cells, which in turn activates p53, impairs the SLC7A11–GPX4 antioxidant axis, and drives lethal lipid peroxidation, ultimately leading to ferroptotic cell death. This mode of action results in potent antitumor efficacy against U87MG glioblastoma both in vitro and in vivo. This work establishes STEAP3 as a key molecular target for photodynamic therapy and proposes a mechanistically defined selenium photosensitizer that overcomes cancer apoptosis resistance by inducing ferroptosis.

title: Rapid vaterite-mediated shell repair for acid-induced damage in a deep-sea mussel
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Mollusks are able to secrete and repair the most diverse and complex calcareous tissues in the animal kingdom, yet the detailed molecular mechanisms of these biomineralization processes, especially for the deep-sea calcifiers, remain to be elucidated. Here, using an in situ experiment, we report a repair mechanism for acid-induced shell damage via biologically mediated vaterite formation in the deep-sea cold-seep mussel
                    Gigantidas haimaensis
                    . Interestingly, the mussels secreted and recrystallized amorphous calcium carbonate into vaterite to seal the acid-induced dissolution porosities within 30 h. Calcium and nucleation substrates were potentially supplied by the mantle, including calcium-binding proteins and hydroxyapatite. Calcium then reacted with readily available carbonate in the extrapallial space, whose precipitation can be promoted by the nucleation substrates. This rapid repair mechanism is likely an advantage in the habitat of these mussels, which are characterized by pulsed acidification events from the seeping fluids. Furthermore, our finding expands our understanding of the diverse biomineralization mechanisms by which mollusks maintain their protective shells.

title: History-dependent droplet friction driven by contact-line aging
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The motion of liquid droplets on solid surfaces is commonly described by contact-line friction, which is generally assumed to increase monotonically with instantaneous velocity. However, such a velocity-only description cannot explain why static droplet friction can exceed dynamic friction or why contact-line friction can become velocity-weakening. Here, we demonstrate that contact-line friction depends jointly on sliding velocity and contact history. Using self-assembled alkylsilane monolayers as molecularly tunable substrates and ionic liquids as low-volatility model liquids, we observe pronounced history-dependent strengthening of contact-line friction on solid-like monolayers, manifested as time-enhanced static friction and velocity-weakening dynamic friction. Both effects are progressively suppressed as the surface is tuned toward a more liquid-like state with a lower density of pinning defects, either by reducing the monolayer chain length or by increasing temperature. We attribute this behavior to nanoscopic contact-line aging, whereby contact-line segments thermally fluctuate and progressively occupy interfacial defects, leading to a progressive increase in contact-line pinning. An aging-based model quantitatively captures the history-dependent onset friction and the low-velocity friction dynamics in our system, while similar logarithmic strengthening across diverse liquid–substrate systems suggests broader applicability of the constitutive framework. These findings establish the coupled effects of contact history and sliding velocity on contact-line friction, extending dynamic wetting beyond velocity-only descriptions and providing a physical basis for controlling macroscopic droplet transport through nanoscale interfacial design.

title: Millennial-scale variability in Greenland dust provenance during Dansgaard–Oeschger events of the last glacial period
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Greenland ice-core records show an approximately 15-fold increase in dust concentration during cold stadial periods compared to warmer interstadial periods in the last glacial period (LGP). While multiple regions including East Asian deserts and the Sahara have been suggested as potential source areas (PSAs) for Greenland dust, millennial-scale variability of their relative contributions associated with Dansgaard–Oeschger climatic fluctuations during the LGP remains poorly constrained. To address this, we investigate high-resolution (~800 y) Pb and Sr isotopic, mineralogical, and geochemical records from the North Greenland Eemian Ice Drilling ice-core samples covering the entire LGP. We found that the Pb and Sr isotopic compositions, kaolinite-to-chlorite ratios, and chemical index of alteration values were higher during stadials than during interstadials. Comparison with PSAs suggests that East Asian deserts remained the dominant contributors to Greenland dust throughout the LGP, but contributions from the Sahara increased during stadial intervals. This shift likely reflects climate-driven changes in atmospheric circulation patterns responsible for transporting dust to Greenland. Our findings provide insights into the relationship between dust cycle dynamics and abrupt climate changes on millennial timescales during the LGP.

title: Active and passive crowding pathways drive topological and mechanical divergence in myoblasts
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Cell crowding is closely associated with many physiological processes, yet our understanding of crowded tissue organization has been developed largely in polygonal epithelia, leaving intrinsically anisotropic cell collectives comparatively poorly understood. Using C2C12 myoblasts, we investigate this problem by decoupling the final crowded state from the pathway taken to reach it, comparing active crowding, arising from cell proliferation during incubation, with passive crowding, imposed directly through high-density seeding. Unlike polygonal epithelia, crowded myoblast monolayers do not undergo epithelial-like kinetic arrest: cell motion is strongly suppressed, yet local rearrangements persist and packing remains structurally irregular. However, the two crowding pathways generate distinct collective states, differing in nematic order and junctional coupling. By contrasting these states, we reveal a close interplay among cell geometry, intercellular coupling, tissue-scale nematic order, and force transmission. This mechanical coordination ultimately shapes physiological function, preserving sensitivity to topographical cues and promoting efficient, spatially organized myogenic fusion. These findings broaden the physical framework of collective organization in active matter and establish key mechanical principles for in vitro tissue engineering.

title: Generating interesting scientific ideas using knowledge graphs and LLMs: Evaluations with 100 research group leaders
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The rapid growth of scientific literature makes it increasingly challenging for researchers to identify novel and impactful ideas, especially across disciplines. Modern AI systems offer new opportunities for scientific ideation, but how compelling are AI-generated ideas, and how can their quality be improved? Here, we introduce
                    SCIMUSE
                    , which generates personalized research ideas using a knowledge graph of 58 million papers and a large language model (LLM). A central focus of this work is to understand how interesting these ideas are. Therefore, we conducted a large-scale evaluation in which more than 100 research group leaders—spanning the natural sciences to the humanities—rated over 4,400 personalized ideas according to their level of interest. Overall, expert ratings were modest (mean 2.40 on a 5-point scale, most common rating 1), while 24.9% of ideas were rated 4 or 5. We find that supplying concept pairs selected using the knowledge graph does not improve expert-rated interest over a titles-only GPT baseline. High-citation-predicted pairs even showed a weak tendency (1.94
                    σ
                    ) toward lower interest than random pairs. Nevertheless, graph features can be used to control properties of ideas, and, using this unique evaluation dataset, we show that idea interest can be predicted with both a supervised neural network based on graph features and a zero-shot ranking approach based on an LLM. Our work provides an AI methodology for generating scientific ideas and a large-scale interdisciplinary expert evaluation, paving the way to study and improve difficult-to-measure metrics such as expert-perceived scientific interestingness.

title: Optimal scenario design for climate emulation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: As deep learning for physical systems continues to grow in popularity, efforts to improve generalizability have primarily focused on designing architectures that embed physical constraints. However, for machine-learning surrogate climate models (emulators), we show that the low structural diversity in existing scenarios commonly used to generate training data places a ceiling on predictive skill. Here, we examine whether training datasets themselves can be optimized to improve generalization. We introduce a method to create datasets that produce emulators capable of generalizing to new, structurally different scenarios absent from the training data. We use a differentiable simple climate model (SCM) to calculate the sensitivity of emulator loss to perturbations in the training data, iteratively updating the training data to maximize emulator skill. For an SCM, an emulator trained on one scenario optimized in this fashion outperforms an emulator trained on six standard Scenario Model Intercomparison Project (ScenarioMIP) pathways. We achieve this higher predictive skill despite training on a smaller dataset, finding that our emulator successfully isolates distinct physical behaviors of different climate forcing agents (e.g., greenhouse gases vs. aerosols) without single-forcing runs. We then demonstrate that scenarios optimized using an SCM, when used to drive an intermediate-complexity climate model, produce a training dataset that yields a more skillful emulator than training on ScenarioMIP outputs. Our results suggest that, in the compute-constrained environment of running full-scale climate models, generating a small number of dynamically rich scenarios provides greater marginal value for emulation and characterizing system responses than expanding the suite of traditional emissions pathways.

title: Structural basis of hypervariable region 1 dynamics on HCV envelope glycoproteins in immune evasion
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The hypervariable region 1 (HVR1) of the hepatitis C virus E1E2 glycoprotein plays a crucial role in immune evasion through rapid mutation and shielding of conserved neutralizing epitopes. Despite its important role, the structural properties of HVR1 remain poorly understood, particularly how its conformation influences shielding mechanisms and receptor recognition. To date in all published E1E2 or E2 structures, the C-terminal part of HVR1 (394 to 411) remains unresolved. Using neutralizing antibody (nAb) RM1-38, which targets C-terminal HVR1 (residues 399 to 409), we investigated the folding, positioning, flexibility, and shielding function of the RM1-38 epitope, or antigenic site 399 (AS399), on HVR1 by X-ray crystallography and negative-stain electron microscopy (nsEM). The crystal structure of RM1-38 Fab with the HVR1 AS399 peptide, combined with mutagenesis analysis, delineated the molecular basis of its strain-specific recognition and neutralization. nsEM and competition enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay revealed that HVR1 exhibits pronounced conformational flexibility even in the presence of other nAbs bound to E1E2. Virus neutralization assays using a combination of RM1-38 and broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) demonstrated antagonistic effects of RM1-38 with the bnAbs. Furthermore, RM1-38 reduced E1E2 binding to cells expressing the scavenger receptor SR-BI, an HVR1-dependent receptor, but did not affect binding to CD81 tetraspanin. Together, these findings support a model in which HVR1 functions as a dynamic shield, where its conformational plasticity contributes to both receptor engagement and evasion of humoral immunity in persistent infection.

title: Signaling mechanism of the transmembrane energy receptor Aer
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The
                    Escherichia coli
                    aerotaxis receptor Aer is a bacterial chemoreceptor that senses intracellular redox changes via an N-terminal PAS domain bound to a flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) cofactor. Distinct from canonical methyl-accepting chemotaxis proteins (MCPs) such as Tar/Tsr, Aer lacks a periplasmic ligand-binding domain and adaptive methylation, transmitting conformational signals laterally from the PAS domain to the HAMP domain and the methylation helix-like cap (MHL-cap) of the kinase control domain (KCD). To elucidate the Aer signaling mechanism, we determined cryoelectron microscopy structures of full-length Aer in oxidized flavin quinone (kinase-on) and reduced semiquinone (kinase-off) states. Structural comparison reveals redox-linked rearrangements of the FAD-binding pocket, reorientation of PAS–HAMP interactions, and strikingly altered MHL-cap stability. PAS–MHL-cap interactions in the oxidized state compress the receptor and stabilize the proximal KCD helices, whereas reduction disrupts these contacts, increasing KCD flexibility. To probe distal effects on KCD architecture, we performed nanodisc reconstitution and pulse dipolar ESR spectroscopy on spin-labeled positions along the four-helix bundle. Distance distributions indicate redox-dependent changes in helix separation, particularly at the C-terminal MHL2 region, consistent with PAS-driven loosening of KCD packing in kinase-off states. These data support a model in which FAD redox chemistry reorganizes flavin pocket residues that in turn subtly alter PAS conformation to influence PAS–HAMP and PAS–MHL-cap packing and hence KCD conformational stability. The findings reveal an Aer-specific signaling axis distinct from periplasmic-ligand binding MCPs that has adapted MCP architecture for lateral PAS input and cytoplasmic redox sensing.

title: Intensification of compound wind drought and heatwave events under climate change
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Compound wind drought and heatwave (WDHW) events, defined as the co-occurrence of low wind speeds and high temperatures, pose growing risks to future power system stability. Yet their future evolution and underlying physical drivers remain poorly constrained. Using daily output from 27 downscaled CMIP6 models (~25 km), we identify a widespread intensification of these compound events over global land areas. Across the low- to high-CO
                    2
                    scenarios, global event frequency is projected to increase by 100 to 750% by 2100, with event duration lengthening by 80 to 300%. Mechanistically, this intensification is mainly driven by thermodynamic warming and widespread wind stilling, and further amplified regionally by enhanced climate variability and strengthened wind–temperature coupling associated with poleward jet streams. Applying an emergent-constraint framework that links observed historical trends to future projections can reduce intermodel variance by 10 to 40% at both global and regional scales. These results provide a physically grounded assessment of future compound WDHW risks, with direct implications for climate-impact assessment and energy-system planning.

abstract:

                    VM

                    VM

                    +

                    super-high

                    VM

Mechanistically, DUSP2 interacts with the replication protein A (RPA) complex to regulate RPA2 phosphorylation and chromatin association. Disruption of the DUSP2–RPA axis promotes R-loop accumulation and increases chromatin accessibility, which in turn activates Eomesodermin (EOMES)-associated transcriptional programs, eventually promoting T

                    VM

title: High‐Density Pixelated Metasurfaces for Terahertz Hyperspectral Imaging
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Metasurface‐enabled terahertz imaging and spectroscopy are moving toward compact, high‐throughput systems, but current approaches remain limited by discrete spectral sampling, computational reconstruction, and the trade‐off between spatial resolution and resonance quality in nonlocal designs. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different paradigm based on photonic crystal heterojunction‐enabled pixelated metasurfaces that directly encode spatial information into spectrally resolved, high‐quality‐factor resonances. By embedding bound‐state‐in‐the‐continuum metapixels within a bandgap‐engineered heterostructure, we simultaneously suppress lateral leakage and control vertical radiation, enabling effective three‐dimensional photon confinement in finite metasurfaces. This mechanism overcomes the conventional dependence of resonance quality on pixel size, yielding enhanced quality factors and figure of merit without increasing the device footprint, and enabling metapixels with lateral dimensions of ∼2λ that retain high spectral fidelity and signal‐to‐noise ratio. Leveraging this capability, we realize a 3 × 3 pixelated metasurface supporting nine independently addressable resonances, all retrieved in a single‐shot broadband terahertz measurement. The resulting spectral‐spatial encoding strategy establishes a direct one‐to‐one mapping between resonance signatures and spatial pixels, enabling hyperspectral imaging with a single‐pixel detector and a THz pulse, without raster scanning or algorithmic inversion. These results provide a scalable route toward real‐time terahertz imaging and integrated photonic sensing.

title: Bismuth‐Mediated Zinc Extraction‐Induced Carbon Defects Boost Fe Single‐Atom Catalysis for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Fe single‐atom catalysts with Fe‐N 4 configurations typically suffer from excessive adsorption of oxygenated intermediates, leading to intrinsic limitations in catalytic efficiency. Here, we propose a Bi‐mediated Fe‐adjacent Zn extraction strategy to create defects adjacent to Fe‐N 4 moieties on ZIF‐8‐derived carbon support, thereby tailoring the local microenvironment of Fe single atoms. The resulting Fe‐N‐pC d catalyst exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity in alkaline electrolyte, delivering a half‐wave potential of 0.918 V versus RHE along with excellent durability. The assembled quasi‐solid‐state Zn‐air battery using Fe‐N‐pC d as the air cathode catalyst affords stable operation for over 3000 h at −40°C. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that the formed carbon defects adjacent to Fe‐N 4 sites redistribute the local electron density and favor the formation of an axial *OH‐bound Fe state under ORR conditions. This defect‐modulated coordination environment lowers the Fe d‐band center and alleviates the overly strong Fe‐*OH coupling, thereby changing the potential‐limiting step from *OH removal to *OOH formation and accelerating ORR kinetics. This study provides a neighboring‐template extraction route for engineering defect microenvironments adjacent to metal single atoms, opening new opportunities for the design of efficient ORR electrocatalysts.

title: Data‐Driven Host Microstructure Design Toward Efficient and Durable Room‐Temperature Sodium–Sulfur Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Porous carbon materials are critical hosts for chalcogen‐ and halogen‐based conversion‐type cathodes, as they govern the activity and durability of electrochemical reactions. Understanding how their microstructures regulate electrolyte‐electrode interactions remains challenging given multiple coupling factors and dynamic changes during electrochemical cycling. Herein, machine learning was first used to screen three pore structure parameter windows relevant to electrochemical features from a large experimental dataset (23 carbon hosts and 1055 specific‐capacity data points). Based on these screened windows, three representative carbon hosts, namely micropore‐rich carbon, balanced carbon, and meso/macropore‐rich carbon, were synthesized as model systems. We reveal that pore structure governs sulfur species evolution, thereby dictating the competition between polysulfide‐mediated reactions and solvent self‐decomposition. The resulting spatial‐compositional differences of the cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) were found to profoundly impact energy efficiency, reversibility, and rate performance. The balanced carbon cathode with optimized inorganic‐organic distribution delivers an initial capacity of 1249.4 mAh g −1 and retains a capacity of 784.8 mAh g −1 after 500 cycles. This work not only proposes a data‐driven strategy for identifying CEI‐relevant pore structure windows, but also provides mechanistic insight into how physical metrics of porous carbon modulate multi‐step complex reactions and ultimately influence electrochemical performance.

title: Understanding Charge Acceptance Limitations During Extreme Fast‐Charging of Li‐ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Extreme fast charging in lithium‐ion batteries is limited by their poor charge acceptance at high C‐rates. We use overpotential component analysis to decouple ohmic, kinetic and transport voltage losses during fast charging. The concentration gradients are identified as the primary culprit in poor charge acceptance, so we study carbonate electrolytes that utilize acetonitrile, a low viscosity, high dielectric liquid, as a co‐solvent to improve ion transport. Our results indicate acetonitrile co‐solvent successfully reduces fast charging concentration gradients and therefore improves charge acceptance at high C‐rates, particularly when used in combination with interface‐stabilizing additives. Molecular dynamics simulations show that ACN enhances Li + transport through a combination of reduced bulk viscosity and increased solvation‐shell lability, with shorter solvent residence times and faster coordination exchange producing transport gains beyond those expected from viscosity reduction alone. Finally, we use three‐electrode cells to deconvolute overpotential at each electrode, and the specific LiNi 0.8 Mn 0.1 Co 0.1 O 2 (NMC811) electrode architecture and loading used in our study is found to have much higher overpotentials than our graphite electrode. In particular, the significant differences in NMC811 concentration gradients between electrolytes with or without acetonitrile indicate that the design of electrode architecture is crucial for extreme fast charging applications.

title: cis–trans Isomerism Enables Visible Light‐Excited Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence and Dynamic Afterglow
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Isomerism serves as a powerful strategy for modulating organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP), which is crucial for developing novel RTP materials and elucidating structure‐property relationships. However, cis – trans isomerism that is widespread in organic compounds has not been deeply explored in terms of its influence on RTP properties. In this study, the cis – trans isomers of two 9,10‐dihydrophenanthrene‐9,10‐dicarbonitriles, DPCN‐H and DPCN‐O (with OMe group), are designed and synthesized. Significant differences in luminous behavior are observed between the cis‐ and trans ‐isomers. The trans ‐DPCNs exhibit notably superior RTP and afterglow performance compared to cis ‐DPCNs for their better structural planarity and tighter packing. Among them, trans ‐DPCN‐O achieves an afterglow quantum yield as high as 43% upon visible‐light excitation. Additionally, trans ‐DPCN‐H displays excitation‐power‐dependent and temperature‐dependent afterglow color modulation, while the nanoparticles of trans ‐DPCN‐O demonstrates efficient visible‐light‐excited afterglow in aqueous solution. The excellent RTP properties of the trans‐ DPCNs enable their successful application in complex anti‐counterfeiting with four dimensions, and in vivo imaging in mice under white LED excitation with a signal‐to‐noise ratio of up to 228. This work presents the first investigation into how cis – trans isomerism affects organic RTP and provides new insights into designing high‐performance RTP materials.

title: Coordination Number‐Tuned FeNx Single‐Atom Nanozymes for Sustained Peroxidase‐Like Catalysis in Tumor Therapy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Peroxidase (POD)‐like catalysis by single‐atom nanozymes (SAEs) under sustained H 2 O 2 exposure requires both rapid substrate activation and durable catalytic turnover, both of which are closely linked to the coordination environment of metal sites. However, how the coordination number governs their balance remains unclear, especially when the interaction strength between SAEs and H 2 O 2 is tuned. Herein, we construct three structurally comparable FeN x ‐SAEs (x = 4, 3, and 2), revealing a volcano‐like relationship between POD‐like activity and H 2 O 2 adsorption strength. The selected FeN 3 ‐SAE exhibits the highest POD‐like activity (1.52 × 10 −6 M s −1 ), which is 1.9‐ and 4.1‐fold greater than those of FeN 2 ‐SAE and FeN 4 ‐SAE, respectively. Moreover, the FeN 3 ‐SAE sustains efficient H 2 O 2 consumption and robust •OH generation during prolonged catalysis, whereas the FeN 4 ‐SAE suffers from inadequate H 2 O 2 activation, and the FeN 2 ‐SAE undergoes rapid kinetic decay. Combined experiments and theoretical calculations attribute this performance to well‐balanced H 2 O 2 adsorption at the FeN 3 site, which facilitates substrate activation, intermediate desorption, and active‐site regeneration. Both cellular and animal experiments reveal that FeN 3 ‐SAE enables continuous H 2 O 2 conversion into cytotoxic •OH, depleting GSH and triggering tumor suppression accompanied by immune activation. This study provides mechanistic insights into sustained POD‐like catalysis from the perspective of coordination number‐regulated adsorption‒turnover balance.

title: A Closed‐Loop‐Recyclable Liquid‐Crystalline Dynamic Covalent Network Soft Actuator Derived From Nonliquid‐Crystalline Monomers
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid‐crystalline networks constructed from nonliquid‐crystalline precursors offer an alternative to conventional routes based on liquid‐crystalline monomers, that is, mesogenic monomers. Here, we report a closed‐loop recyclable liquid crystal polymer network (CLLCP) synthesized from nonliquid‐crystalline aldehyde and amine building blocks through reversible imine chemistry. Imine formation constructs mesogenic segments and establishes network connectivity, linking liquid‐crystalline structural design with chemical recyclability. This approach avoids pre‐synthesis of liquid‐crystalline monomers and offers flexibility in the selection of network components. The combination of rigid imine‐linked segments and flexible spacers supports liquid‐crystalline order and segmental mobility, while dynamic imine bonds enable stress relaxation and thermal reprocessing. Aligned CLLCP films exhibit a reversible thermomechanical actuation strain of 26% with good cycling stability. Under acidic conditions, imine hydrolysis disassembles the network and enables recovery of the four original molecular building blocks. These components are reused to reconstruct networks with phase behavior, mechanical properties, and actuation performance comparable to those of the pristine materials. This molecular design couples in situ mesogenic‐segment construction with polymer‐to‐monomer closed‐loop recycling, providing a modular route to sustainable liquid‐crystalline soft actuators.

Diffusion Models for Small-Molecule Design
abstract: Abstract Diffusion models (DMs) have emerged as a class of generative models for controllable small-molecule design in drug discovery capable of progressively transforming noisy or partially specified molecular states into candidate structures under structural, geometric, and property constraints. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of the methodological foundations and representative applications of diffusion-based molecular generation, emphasizing the alignment among molecular representations, generative dynamics, controllable design, and evaluation and validation. Particular attention is given to recent advances in property- and structure-guided generation, target-aware and fragment-based design, multiobjective optimization, and synthesis-aware generation. We also discuss the roles of data sets, computational evaluation, and prospective experiments in assessing the chemical and biological relevance of generated molecules. By organizing these developments within a unified conceptual framework, we provide computational chemists and drug discovery researchers with a structured roadmap that balances the mathematical rigor with chemical intuition. Throughout, we highlight current methodological limitations and unresolved challenges and conclude with future directions toward chemically credible and experimentally grounded molecular design. To facilitate navigation of this rapidly evolving field, we introduce an interactive companion platform (https://diffsmd.scbdd.com) that provides a curated, continuously updated repository of model architectures and visualizations.

title: Mesoscale Chiroptical Order in Achiral Metal-Halide Nanoplatelet Assemblies
abstract: Abstract This viewpoint presents the circular dichroism emerging directly from the self-assembly of achiral metal-halide perovskite nanoplatelets such as Cs3Cd2Cl7, Rb3Cd2Cl7, and CsPbBr3. Specifically, even when they form only short-range, polydisperse assemblies rather than the long-range helical superlattices reported in prior works, these short assemblies also exhibit chiral optical properties. The effect persists across emissive and nonemissive systems; with diverse stacking morphologies, and both in solution and film forms. Thus, this viewpoint establishes mesoscale chirality as a general principle of nanoplatelet self-assemblies.

title: Rational Selection of Hole Contacts with an Organic Light-Emitting Diode Industry p-Dopant for Fully Vacuum-Processed Perovskite/Silicon Tandems
abstract: Abstract Translating perovskite/silicon tandems to fully vacuum-based manufacturing requires vacuum-compatible p-doped hole contacts, yet clear selection criteria for doped hole-transport materials (HTMs) remain underdeveloped compared with C60-based electron contacts. Here, we report a fully vacuum-processed perovskite/silicon tandem reaching 29.1% power conversion efficiency, among the highest reported for tandems with fully vacuum-deposited perovskite top cells, enabled by transferring the organic light-emitting diode (OLED)-industry p-dopant NDP-9 and an evaporable arylamine HTM into the perovskite stack. Comparing TaTm, Spiro-TTB, and TAPC shows that contact selection does not follow apparent host–dopant interaction strength derived from theoretical calculations or conventional optical, vibrational, and photoemission spectroscopies. Instead, device-level charge extraction and recombination metrics identify NDP-9-doped TaTm as the most effective contact, also yielding 20.0% in a single-junction 1.70 eV wide-bandgap cell. These results point to transport-based screening as a practical route to selecting vacuum-compatible doped hole contacts.

title: Operando Time-of-Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry Reveals Iodine-Mediated Redox Chemistry in Solid-State Li–S Batteries
abstract: Abstract Understanding dynamic reaction pathways in all-solid-state batteries remains challenging because electrochemical processes occur at buried solid–solid interfaces and transient intermediates are difficult to detect with conventional analytical techniques. While operando techniques typically probe structural or macroscopic changes, direct detection of reactive species during operation remains experimentally demanding. Here, we introduce a dynamic operando time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry platform that enables continuous chemical analysis of processes in a solid-state battery under electrochemical bias. Using this approach, we directly observe a pronounced increase of the I2– signal during charging of a Li–S composite cathode containing LiI, indicating the formation of elemental iodine. Concurrent changes in the sulfur-containing ion signals suggest the involvement of iodine species in the ongoing redox processes. These results reveal transient, low-concentration species at buried interfaces undetectable by other operando techniques, offering a pathway for identifying reactive intermediates in conversion-type solid-state batteries and related electrochemical systems.

title: Decoding Symmetry-Breaking Band Structures in Nanocatalysts for Kinetically Favorable Li-S Batteries
abstract: Abstract The conventional d-band center theory represents catalyst electronic structures using an averaged energy and may therefore overlook higher-order information contained in the complex and asymmetric density of states of alloy catalysts (ACs). Here, combining quantum chemistry with interpretable machine learning, we identify the transformed d-band peak position (Epp) as an alternative electronic descriptor for alloy–polysulfide interactions in lithium-sulfur batteries. Epp integrates information related to the d-band position, bandwidth, and band shape, and correlates with the electron occupation of S3p–Md (M = metal) antibonding states and the calculated polysulfide adsorption strength. A series of bimetallic ACs recovered from spent lithium-ion batteries was employed to experimentally evaluate the descriptor. Within this series, CoFe shows favorable electrochemical performance, enabling an ampere-hour-level pouch cell with an energy density of 426 Wh kg–1 under a sulfur loading of 12.5 mg cm–2 and an electrolyte-to-sulfur ratio of 3.6 mL g–1.

title: Dye-Sensitization Enables Visible-Light-Driven N–N Bond Cleavage in a Dinuclear Rhenium Dinitrogen Complex
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Conversion of μ-N2 complexes into nitrogenous compounds is one of the most important and challenging chemical transformations in N2 fixation. Although photochemical N2 splitting has been demonstrated, existing approaches predominantly rely on high-energy ultraviolet light that generally affords low efficiency and poor selectivity. Herein, we establish a visible-light-driven molecular photosensitization strategy that enables efficient and selective N–N bond cleavage in a dinuclear rhenium dinitrogen complex. Blue light excitation of the organic photosensitizer 4DPAIPN (2,4,5,6-tetrakis(diphenylamino)isophthalonitrile) is shown to initiate N–N scission to afford the corresponding rhenium nitride in 96% yield. Kinetic analysis of nanosecond transient absorption data through the Balzani-Scandola model indicates energy transfer from the photosensitizer to an acceptor state that lies approximately 2.31 eV above the ground state of the μ-N2-bridged dirhenium complex. This photosensitization strategy decouples light harvesting from N–N bond activation, eliminates the need for UV light, and shows broad applicability across different visible-light absorbing photosensitizers, including transition metal complexes and organic chromophores with long-lived, high-energy triplet excited-states. These findings establish dye-sensitization as a powerful strategy for visible-light-driven N–N bond cleavage for mechanistic study and the future realization of a photochemical pathway for nitrogen fixation.

title: Design and Evolution of an Orthogonal HaloTag for Multiplexed Labeling in Cells
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The self-labeling protein HaloTag is used to install a wide variety of functional small molecules in cells and living organisms with exquisite specificity with respect to cell type and subcellular localization. HaloTag is a core part of many biotechnology-based tools for sensing, tracking, and manipulating biological systems with a high degree of spatial and temporal control. Due to the limitations of fluorescent proteins and other self-labeling proteins, most of these tools have historically been restricted to a single channel. In this work, we used structure-guided rational design and directed evolution to produce an orthogonal HaloTag protein called OrthoTag which reacts selectively with a modified chloroalkane substrate. OrthoTag retains many of HaloTag’s superior properties, and reaction rate measurements with purified proteins show OrthoTag and its substrate have 109-fold mutual orthogonality to HaloTag with respect to substrate concentration. We demonstrate the application of OrthoTag for multiplexed labeling experiments in mammalian cells with minimal optimization. Going forward, OrthoTag should be straightforward to incorporate into HaloTag-based systems to allow simultaneous measurement or manipulation of two biological targets or processes. The availability of multiple high-performance self-labeling proteins will enable the continued development of new multiplexed biotechnology methods.

title: Programming Oxygen Reduction Selectivity via Peroxo Basicity: Acid-Controlled 2e–/4e– Reduction Switching at a Dicobalt Platform
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Achieving switchable 2e–/4e– oxygen reduction selectivity within a single molecular catalyst remains an unmet challenge because the key metal–oxygen intermediate typically commits to one pathway. Herein, we demonstrate that this limitation can be overcome by elevating the basicity of the peroxo intermediate to a level where both proton-transfer (PT) and proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) manifolds become accessible, with the dominant pathway dictated solely by the external acid strength. A dicobalt μ-1,2-peroxo complex supported by an electron-rich macrocyclic poly-NHC ligand exhibits a computed pKa1 of ∼8.8, placing it in a unique thermodynamic window. Stoichiometric protonation bifurcates cleanly: strong acids (HClO4) trigger rapid diprotonation to release H2O2, whereas weak acids (Et3NHOTf) promote O–O bond cleavage to afford a μ-hydroxo complex. Under catalytic conditions, this dichotomy translates into complete selectivity switching─100% H2O2 with HClO4 versus 90% H2O with Et3NHOTf, accompanied by a switch in the rate-determining step from O2 binding to PCET (KIE = 1.60). Crucially, a structurally analogous but less basic peroxo complex predictably inverts the selectivity to H2O under identical conditions, providing a closed-loop validation of the basicity-selectivity relationship. These results establish intermediate basicity as a general, tunable design parameter for programming product selectivity in multielectron catalysis.

title: Synthesis and Crystal Structure of Bulk Methanetetrol C(OH)4
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Methanetetrol, C(OH)4 (orthocarbonic acid), is an elusive tethrahydroxymethane that, due to its rapid dissociation under ambient conditions, has never been synthesized in bulk. A recent study detected the formation of C(OH)4 molecules in the gas phase. Here, we show that C(OH)4 can be synthesized in a diamond anvil cell through the reaction between H2O and CO2 at 45(3) GPa and 50(3) GPa and temperatures

title: Multiphase Inorganic-Rich Interphases with Integrated Li-Ion Capture-Transport Ability for High-Rate Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Lithium metal batteries promise high-energy-density storage but are limited by unstable solid–electrolyte interphases, which couple poor passivation, sluggish Li+ transport, dendritic deposition, and safety risks. Herein, we report a multiphase inorganic-rich solid–electrolyte interphase (m-SEI) containing P- and Al-derived species including Li3P, LiAl5O8, Li3PO4, and Li2Al, which is formed from the in situ reaction between a flame-retardant aluminum diethyl hypophosphite (ADP) interlayer and lithium metal. This multicomponent inorganic SEI enables an integrated capture-transport mechanism by combining high Li+ affinity, facilitated desolvation, and low-barrier Li+ migration pathways in individual inorganic phases and their heterophase interfaces, thereby facilitating rapid Li+ interfacial migration. Its chemical inertness and high Young’s modulus of 17.14 GPa further suppress electrolyte decomposition and Li dendrite growth. As a result, the Li-metal batteries with m-SEI deliver an extended lifespan of 1000 h at a high current density of 4 mA cm–2. Li||NCM811 full cells with a high cathode loading (20 mg cm–2) and ultrathin Li foil (50 μm) retain 80% capacity after 250 cycles, while Li||NCM811 pouch cells retain 90% capacity after 500 cycles. This work establishes the capture-transport mechanism as an effective design principle for regulating Li+ interfacial dynamics and offers a practical interphase-engineering strategy for constructing ion-conductive and chemically protective interphases in durable lithium metal batteries.

title: Tailoring Solid-State Reaction Pathways for Bulk Fluorination of Mn-Rich Rock-Salt Cathodes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Manganese-based cation-disordered rock-salt (DRX) cathodes offer high capacities without relying on cobalt and nickel, but maintaining that capacity over extended cycling often requires bulk fluorination. The challenge is that incorporating fluorine into Mn-rich DRX host structures is hindered by unfavorable thermodynamics and the stability of LiF, often necessitating elevated synthesis temperatures that promote severe lithium and fluorine volatilization. This study overcomes that limitation by manipulating the solid-state reaction pathway using unconventional Li6MnO4 and MnF2 precursors in a challenging Mn-rich model system (Li1.2Mn0.6Ti0.2O2–xFx). This precursor engineering strategy reshapes the thermodynamic landscape. Computational modeling and in situ X-ray diffraction reveal that by using reactive starting materials, we suppress the crystallization of less reactive intermediates, enabling bulk fluorination at a lower temperature. The resulting DRX retains both a high fluorine content and the lithium excess required for three-dimensional percolation, delivering improved electrochemical performance relative to material synthesized from conventional precursors.

title: Hydration-Dependent Working-Surface Chemistry in Photocatalytic Methane Coupling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Selective photocatalytic methane coupling requires directing methane-derived intermediates toward C–C bond formation while limiting their oxidation to CO2, yet how the reaction environment controls this competition through surface chemistry remains unclear. Water is ubiquitous in photocatalytic methane conversion, but its influence is commonly interpreted through specific chemical functions rather than through its broader effects on working-surface chemistry. Here, Au/ZnO is used as a compositionally defined, coupling-competent model catalyst to reveal how hydration regulates carbon transformation pathways by reshaping the working-surface chemistry. Systematic variation of water availability reveals three hydration-dependent catalytic regimes with markedly different product distributions. Moderate hydration increases the ethane production rate from 1590 to 8407 μmol g–1 h–1 and enables ethylene formation, whereas excessive hydration increases CO2 production and lowers C2 selectivity. In situ spectroscopies show that these catalytic regimes are accompanied by hydration-dependent changes in methane adsorption, methane-derived and coupling-related surface intermediates, and oxygen-deficient surface states within a reaction network involving both carbon- and oxygen-centered radical chemistry. Moderate hydration establishes surface conditions that favor C–C coupling and C2 hydrocarbon accumulation, whereas excessive hydration favors oxidized surface species and carbonate formation. These results identify hydration as a key determinant of the steady-state surface chemistry governing carbon partitioning between C–C coupling and oxidation during photocatalytic methane conversion.

title: Dynamic Metal Encapsulation in a Pt/TiO x system Regulated by Pt-Assisted TiO2 Amorphization
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Strong metal–support interaction (SMSI) plays an important role in heterogeneous catalysis, but remains poorly understood, particularly on the origin of SMSI under an oxidative atmosphere. Hereby grand canonical structure exploration of over 4 million bulk PtTi alloys and Pt or PtTi-supported Ti oxide (TiOx) surface structure candidates, we resolve the Pt/TiOx system, a text-book example of SMSI, under both reductive and oxidative conditions: it experiences an encapsulation─deep encapsulation─decapsulation dynamic reconstruction under a sequence of H2 reduction─O2 oxidation─H2 plus O2 redox thermal treatment. The whole process was kinetically simulated by long-time (69 ns) molecular dynamics simulations, revealing in detail how a 3 nm Pt nanoparticle undergoes nonclassical SMSI under an oxidative and redox atmosphere. We find that Pt-assisted TiO2 amorphization is the key to the transition of various SMSI states at different conditions, which elevates Ti chemical potential via amorphization toward low-coordinated [TiO4]. Finally, explainable machine learning models were developed to predict nonclassical SMSI cases and clarify their rarity in nature.

title: Efficient Long-Wavelength Through-Space Charge-Transfer Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence in Conformationally Adaptive Emitters without Conformational Locking
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Through-space charge-transfer thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TSCT-TADF) emitters often employ conformationally constrained donor–acceptor architectures to control through-space electronic coupling, particularly for long-wavelength emission. Here, we report conformationally adaptive orange-to-red TSCT-TADF emitters based on an S-shaped donor−π–acceptor−π–donor framework composed of phenoxazine donors, xanthene linkers, and a dibenzo[a,j]phenazine acceptor. Structural and NMR analyses reveal substantial conformational mobility, while systematic conformational searches and excited-state calculations identify thermally accessible conformers with distinct donor–acceptor geometries and excited-state characteristics. Comparative studies with reference compounds and fragment-resolved transition-density analysis show that the xanthene linker primarily acts as a conformational regulator and that the low-energy CT states have predominant TSCT character with only minor linker involvement. Temperature-dependent early-time photoluminescence measurements reveal continuous spectral relaxation in fluid toluene that slows upon cooling and is absent in rigid Zeonex and mCBP hosts, providing strong evidence for structural relaxation following photoexcitation within a pre-existing conformational ensemble. The emitters exhibit orange-to-red TADF with reverse intersystem crossing rates on the order of 105–106 s–1. Organic light-emitting diodes employing these emitters show electroluminescence at 598–624 nm, external quantum efficiencies up to 14.9%, and limited efficiency roll-off over a broad luminance range. These results demonstrate that efficient long-wavelength TSCT-TADF can be realized without permanent conformational locking and establish a framework for understanding the interplay between ground-state conformational heterogeneity and excited-state structural relaxation.

title: Dynamic Acidic Adsorbates Govern Fast Oxygen Incorporation in Ceria through Interfacial Electrostatics
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a key heterogeneous process underpinning energy conversion, catalytic, and sensing technologies. However, reported ORR kinetics at oxide surfaces often vary widely because surface chemistry evolves under operating conditions. Ceria-based fluorites have been proposed as protective layers to stabilize perovskite electrodes, but ORR kinetics are typically considered sluggish and reported values have large variability. Herein, we demonstrate that cathodic polarization triggers an unexpected activation in Gd-doped ceria (CGO) dense thin films at 500 °C, enabling oxygen incorporation rates that surpass state-of-the-art materials such as La0.5Sr0.5FeO3−δ and approach the performance of La0.6Sr0.4CoO3−δ. Operando near-ambient-pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (NAP-XPS), supported by ex situ surface-sensitive tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TERS), reveals that CGO surface activation coincides with a reversible, overpotential-dependent modulation of sulfate adsorbates. Integration of these measurements with nondilute space-charge modeling suggests that charged adsorbates dynamically tune the near-surface electrostatic potential and electron concentration, thereby controlling oxygen incorporation kinetics. These results support adsorbate-induced electrostatic effects as a key mechanism in ceria and show that ORR kinetics are dynamically set by surface chemistry under operation, rather than by intrinsic bulk defect chemistry alone.

title: Photoresponsive Mechanically Interlocked [ a n]Daisy Chain Network
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Muscle integrates molecular-machine motion with hierarchical structural organization, enabling it to sustain large deformations under physiological loads. Mechanically interlocked molecules offer a versatile platform to mimic such molecular-level motion, but efficiently translating it into macroscopic material performance, akin to muscle, remains challenging. Herein, we report a mechanically interlocked network (MIN) with [an]daisy chain backbone which can efficiently scale up the photoresponsive behavior of mechanical bonds, exhibiting intelligently tunable mechanical properties. In specific, photoresponsive unit of arylazopyrazole (AAP) is embedded onto the axis of each mechanical bond in the [an]daisy chain backbone. Ultraviolet light triggers the trans-to-cis (E/Z) isomerization of the AAP moieties, and when amplified through the [an]daisy chain backbone, it brings about significant changes in the material’s properties. On one hand, the E/Z isomerization significantly shortens the dimension of the [an]daisy chain framework, resulting in a notable increase in the material modulus (from 1.6 to 4.0 MPa). On the other hand, the cis configuration of AAP formed after the isomerization restricts the mobility of the mechanical bonds, resulting in a shorter elongation at break (from 343% to 272%). Our work presents an efficient method for amplifying mechanical bond responsiveness, providing a fresh perspective for the development of intelligent materials.

title: Unlocking Intrinsic Chirality in Luminescent Copper Clusters via Intramolecular Spatial Confinement
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Most luminescent clusters that exhibit pronounced chiral signals typically rely on predesigned chiral ligands; however, stimulating the intrinsic chirality of clusters in the absence of exogenous asymmetric ligands remains a significant challenge. In this study, based on a series of structure-correlated Cu2 clusters, we demonstrate that intramolecular spatial confinement effectively induces distortions in flexible ligands, thereby imparting asymmetry to the cluster framework. This molecular asymmetry further determines the orientation of cluster entities during supramolecular assembly, thus enabling the modulation of chirality across this cluster series between inactive (“off”) and active (“on”) states. In addition, these structure-correlated Cu2 clusters display bright and tunable luminescence, allowing for the fabrication of uniform thin films that function as practical scintillation materials for high-resolution X-ray imaging. Collectively, this work provides a novel perspective for regulating the chiroptical properties of metal clusters through the activation of intramolecular spatial confinement and offers valuable insights into the fabrication of cluster-based nanomaterials with tailored photophysical performances.

title: Porphyrin-Driven Redox Tuning in Structurally Defined De Novo Heme Proteins
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Designing redox proteins with predictable and tunable electron transfer properties is a major goal in de novo bioenergetics. Here we show that replacing heme B with a series of structurally conservative non-natural metalloporphyrins enables broad modulation of redox potentials over 400 mV in the de novo designed monoheme m4D2 and diheme 4D2 T19D. The non-natural porphyrins bind with high affinity and do not compromise either the heme binding site or global protein structure, as evidenced by X-ray crystallography and NMR spectroscopy. We also report the native-like NMR structure of m4D2 loaded with the non-natural and symmetric iron 2,4-dimethyldeuteroporphyrin IX, confirming our modular approach to tetrahelical redox protein design. This work establishes a versatile platform for constructing tunable electron carriers for engineered bioenergetic pathways and bioelectronic applications.

title: Reconfigurable Exchange Bias Enabled by Photoresponsive Liquid Crystal Networks in FeGa/IrMn Magnetic Heterostructures
abstract: Abstract Post-fabrication tunability of magnetic properties remains a key challenge for next-generation spintronic and adaptive magneto-electronic devices. Here, we report on a fully electrically contactless strategy to reversibly manipulate the magnetic response of an exchange-biased Ta/Fe80Ga20/Ir20Mn80/Ta multilayer stack through external light stimuli. A photoresponsive azobenzene-doped liquid crystal network (LCN) substrate is employed as an active support for the heterostructure capable of transferring controllable stress to the magnetostrictive FeGa layer under ultraviolet irradiation. This strain-mediated coupling induces a tunable uniaxial magnetic anisotropy in the device, enabling continuous, angular-dependent modulation of key magnetic parameters, including exchange bias and coercivity. Their variation reaches about 11% with respect to the unstressed state. Owing to the slow thermal relaxation kinetics of the LCN, the UV-induced magnetic state is retained after the illumination is switched off over timescales relevant for device operation and can be fully erased by subsequent green-light irradiation. Notably, both the magnitude and sign of the modulation are strongly angle-dependent, reflecting the interplay among stress-induced, magnetocrystalline, and interfacial (i.e., exchange coupling) anisotropies. This approach demonstrates a pathway toward reconfigurable, energy-efficient magnetic systems with remotely tunable functionality, offering significant advantages for miniaturized devices adaptable to dynamic, multi-stimuli environments.

title: In Situ Displacement Reaction Enables a Conductive Metallized Hydrogel Interface for Smart Underwater Flexible Electronics
abstract: Abstract Underwater wearable sensing is severely hampered by the intrinsic drawbacks of conventional materials, including water absorption, swelling, and electrical drift during long-term immersion. Here, we develop an anti-swelling hydrogel with a surface-metallized layer, which achieves strong stability of both mechanical structure and electrical conductivity during long-term underwater immersion. The precise regulation of hydrophilic acrylamide and hydrophobic butyl acrylate enables anti-swelling performance, while an in-situ displacement reaction conveniently and readily constructs an interfacial silver layer on the hydrogel. The hydrogel exhibits remarkable mechanical sensing performance, including high pressure sensitivity, fast response/recovery times, and a broad tensile sensing range. The sensor is integrated into an electronic skin for motion and physiological monitoring (joint bending, respiration, electromyography, and electrocardiography). With AI assistance, this electronic skin achieves 93.75% accuracy in handwriting recognition via a ProbSparse Transformer model. More importantly, a waterproof multichannel sensing system is constructed for real-time monitoring of underwater finger movements and gesture-associated resistance responses. This hydrogel sensor thus serves as a simple, robust, and amphibious platform for healthcare and human-machine interfaces in both air and water.

title: Nanomechanics of MXene Flakes at Gold Interfaces
abstract: Abstract The demand for novel self-powering and sustainable electronics requires major efforts in identifying new advanced materials for nano-applications. MXenes have gathered attention due to their electronic and mechanical properties; however, their nanomechanical compliance against a metal-like interface is still not clearly identified. In this work, we employ atomic force microscopy to characterize the nanomechanical properties of a self-assembled thin flake of titanium carbide MXene (Ti3C2Tx) against a gold probe. The investigation returns an interfacial shear stress of 399 MPa and the observation of nano-wear localized in the center of the MXene flake. Nevertheless, MXene flakes retained their crystallinity in the tribofilms, as confirmed by transmission electron microscopy and electron energy loss spectroscopy. The outcomes of this work set the basis for the use of Ti3C2Tx in novel nano harvesting systems involving metal (e.g., Au) interfaces with large scope in nanoelectronics, wearable sensing, electric vehicles, and robotics.

title: Structural Dynamics of a COF-Based Soft Actuator: Molecular Motion and Macroscopic Response
abstract: Abstract Translating molecular-level dynamics of crystalline frameworks into macroscopic function remains a central challenge in the design of responsive materials. Here, we report that the intrinsic flexibility of COF-300 can be systematically characterized in the bulk powder and then harnessed in a processable composite film to achieve coupled optical and mechanical actuation. In powder form, COF-300 exhibits distinct responses to applied stimuli, including solvent vapors, acid-base environments, and temperature changes. Variable-temperature solid-state NMR reveals the thermally activated coalescence of the phenylene ring signals, and variable-temperature powder X-ray diffraction uncovers colossal anisotropic thermal expansion. Periodic TDA-DFT calculations trace the acid-induced chromism to both geometric distortion and protonation of framework. Embedding COF-300 into a poly(vinylidene fluoride) matrix produces a PVDF@COF film in which solvent vapors drive reversible bending–unbending motion synchronized with a visible color shift, and heating drives the same reversible motion. Exposure to HCl turns the film orange and locks both responses through imine protonation, while thermal deprotonation unlocks them, establishing a reversible chemical switch over framework dynamics. These findings show how molecular flexibility in a crystalline framework can translate into programmable macroscopic actuation, advancing the design of multifunctional solid-state actuators with integrated optical and mechanical output.

title: Decoupling Metal Deposition from Contact Formation Enables Polarity Transformation in WSe2 Transistors
abstract: Abstract Polarity control in two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor field-effect transistors (FETs) is essential for their integration into complementary logic circuits. However, existing polarity-engineering approaches often fail to preserve high-quality contact interfaces because atomically thin 2D semiconductors are highly sensitive to fabrication processes. Here, we introduce an effective buffer-layer removal process that enables polarity transformation while preserving a high-quality contact interface. A thin semimetal layer (Bi or Sb) is deposited prior to high-work-function metal evaporation and subsequently removed by a wet chemical treatment that preserves a high-quality metal/semiconductor interface. Minimizing the contact angle of the rinsing solution suppresses wrinkle and bubble formations and reduces Fermi-level pinning. The same WSe2 transistors transform from semimetal-dominated n-type transport before treatment to high-work-function-metal-dominated p-type transport afterward. Monolayer devices exhibit a maximum two-terminal hole field-effect mobility of 313 cm2 V–1 s–1 after treatment, while also supporting a maximum electron mobility of 41 cm2 V–1 s–1 before treatment. These results demonstrate n-to-p polarity transformation in WSe2 transistors enabled by a removable semimetal layer, providing a potential doping-free route toward complementary 2D electronics.

title: SERS-Active Nanocomposite Contact Lenses for Label-Free Multiplexed Biosensing of Tear Analytes
abstract: Abstract Continuous monitoring remains limited by the fact that most wearable biosensors are built around single-analyte recognition chemistries, even though many physiological states are defined by changes across multiple metabolites. Tear fluid is one of the most biochemically informative biofluids accessible non-invasively, but contact lens biosensors have largely relied on enzymatic or electrochemical techniques that are difficult to extend beyond one target marker at a time. Here, we report a label-free surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS)-active contact lens in which gold nanostars are grown in situ on commercial hydrogel contact lenses. The resulting gold nanostar-loaded contact lens (AuNS-CL) introduces a plasmonic sensing layer directly onto the wearable substrate, with a substrate-averaged SERS enhancement factor of ∼105, while preserving the lens’ physiochemical properties. Quantitative biosensing was demonstrated using a digital thresholding method to account for variable hotspot distributions. Metabolites such as lactate and urea were quantified through their diagnostic bands in several solutions, including artificial tears and a mixture of tear analytes. The AuNS-CLs showed a strong linear response in the physiological range and recovery errors below 10%. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a wearable contact lens for label-free SERS quantification of tear metabolites.

title: Hydrogen-Bond-Regulated PAN/PTFBZ Nanofibrous Composite Barriers for Flame-Resistant Thermal Runaway Protection
abstract: Abstract Electrospun polymer barriers are attractive for lightweight thermal protection in compact lithium–ion battery (LIB) devices, but their limited flame resistance and structural stability under thermal abuse restrict their practical use. Herein, a hydrogen-bond-regulated nanofibrous composite barrier was developed by incorporating trifluoromethyl-modified benzoxazine (TFBZ)-derived components into a polyacrylonitrile (PAN) matrix. The benzoxazine-derived phenolic hydroxyl groups could interact with the nitrile groups of PAN through O–H···N≡C hydrogen bonding, contributing to improved interfacial compatibility and fibrous-network stabilization while retaining the processability of PAN. Thermogravimetric analysis showed that PAN/PTFBZ retained 96.1% of its mass at 300 °C, compared with 75.8% for pure PAN. Cone calorimetry showed that the total heat release and total smoke production were reduced by 64.9% and 45.1%, respectively, and the limiting oxygen index (LOI) increased from 18% to 31%. In battery-level thermal abuse tests, the time to complete thermal runaway (TR) increased from 1068.7 ± 14.6 s to 1884.7 ± 44.2 s, corresponding to 76.4% delay. These results suggest that interfacial hydrogen-bonding regulation, together with the ─CF3-modified benzoxazine-derived structure and compact char formation, contributes to improved flame resistance, structural retention, and battery-level thermal-abuse protection.

title: A Keratin and Polyacrylamide Dual Network Hydrogel Based on Dynamic Coordination between Polydopamine and Mg2+ for Infected Wound Repair
abstract: Abstract Exogenous bacterial infection severely impairs skin wound repair and creates a complex therapeutic challenge that requires simultaneous infection control, oxidative stress regulation, and tissue regeneration. In this study, a PAM/HK/PDANP-Mg2+ multifunctional hydrogel (HPPM) was developed as a cascade therapeutic dressing for infected wounds. In this system, polyacrylamide (PAM) provided a flexible covalently cross-linked framework. Hydrolyzed keratin (HK) offered bioactive and cytocompatible interfaces. Polydopamine nanoparticles (PDANPs) endowed the hydrogel with adhesiveness, photothermal antibacterial activity, and radical scavenging capacity. Coordination between Mg2+ and PDA, together with intermolecular hydrogen bonding, contributed to reversible physical cross-linking within the PAM framework. The optimized HPPM (0.012) hydrogel exhibited a porous structure, high swelling ratio (∼1277%), strong adhesion properties (31.00 kPa), and large tensile elongation (∼560%). Under 808 nm near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, HPPM achieved mild photothermal heating and over 99% antibacterial efficiency against Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus). It also showed favorable antioxidant activity, cytocompatibility, and pro-migratory effects. In an S. aureus-infected rat wound model, HPPM (0.012) + NIR accelerated wound closure, reduced inflammation, enhanced collagen deposition and re-epithelialization, and regulated IL-10/TNF-α expression. These results suggest that HPPM promotes infected wound healing through dynamic coordination-driven cascade remodeling of the infected wound microenvironment.

title: Diffuse Fabry-Pérot Cavities from a Bifunctional Metal Mesh for Angle-Invariant Electrochromic Camouflage
abstract: Abstract Tungsten trioxide (WO3) is a widely studied electrochromic material, yet its monochromatic switching behavior limits its applicability in scenarios requiring dynamic color modulation. To address this limitation, integration with a Fabry-Pérot (F-P) optical cavity has emerged as an effective strategy for expanding color tunability while reducing viewing-angle dependence. In this work, a simplified F-P cavity is constructed using stainless-steel mesh (SSM) as a bifunctional reflector and electrode, with a sputtered WO3 film serving as the electrochromic spacer. This design enables continuous full-spectrum color modulation across the visible range through precise regulation of the WO3 layer thickness. Meanwhile, the microscale topological roughness of the SSM introduces diffuse light scattering, which synergistically couples with F-P interference to compensate for optical path variations at different viewing angles. As a result, angle-independent structural coloration is achieved over a broad viewing-angle range from 15 to 90°. Furthermore, benefiting from the high electrical conductivity and unique porous structure of the SSM, a 14 cm × 14 cm inverted flexible electrochromic device was successfully fabricated. The resulting device exhibits fast switching kinetics, excellent mechanical durability under repeated bending, and stable reversible multicolor performance, demonstrating a scalable and cost-effective platform for adaptive visible-light camouflage and energy-efficient reflective display applications.

title: Porosity Tunable Silk Fibroin Microspheres Enhance Cartilage Repair in Rabbit Model
abstract: Abstract Repairing articular cartilage defects is particularly challenging due to the tissue's hypovascularity and limited intrinsic healing capacity, which pose significant clinical challenges. Biomaterial-based scaffolds have shown promising outcomes in terms of repair capacity; however, finding a robust scaffold system remains challenging in cartilage tissue engineering. In this study, silk fibroin porous microspheres were fabricated using the co-axial electrospraying technique, followed by ethanol treatment to induce crosslinking and enhance microsphere stability. Interestingly, we observed that while changing the ethanol concentration from 100% to 75% to crosslink the silk microsphere resulted in the formation of tunable micropores, with pore sizes up to 87 μm in nonporous microspheres and ranging from 80–200 μm in porous microspheres. Then, we seeded human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hAdMSCs) onto microspheres to evaluate cell adhesion and proliferation over time. The microspheres exhibited enhanced cell adhesion during in vitro cytocompatibility assessments. Notably, porous microspheres displayed superior cell migration compared to nonporous microspheres, attributed to their interconnected pore architecture. Additionally, hAdMSCs-laden microspheres were further studied for their chondrogenic potential under induction conditions, demonstrating cartilage-specific marker expression. Moreover, macroscopic observations and histological staining images showed cartilage regeneration in a rabbit cartilage-defect model, in which porous microspheres outperformed nonporous counterparts due to their enhanced nutrient transfer and host-scaffold integration. Together, these results suggest that silk fibroin microspheres can mimic the extracellular matrix microenvironment, support cell growth, and promote matrix accumulation for effective cartilage repair.

title: Waterborne-Polyurethane as High-Performance Binder for Cathodes of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract In lithium-ion batteries, the electrodes are strongly influenced by the polymer binder swelling in liquid electrolytes, which governs electrode integrity, adhesion, flexibility and Li+ transport. Herein, a series of polyacrylate-terminated waterborne polyurethanes (WPUAs) are designed by systematically varying the proportions of nonionic, anionic, and zwitterionic monomers to regulate swelling behavior in liquid electrolytes. The compositional modulation influences the polymer polarity, polymer entanglement, polymer mechanical property and their swelling in electrolytes, and finally the final electrochemical performance of WPUAs. The optimized WPUA exhibits a balanced swelling ratio, strong adhesion, and significantly enhanced Li+ diffusion. Density functional theory calculation reveals that the molecular configuration is rational and conducive to the Li+ transport, which are supported by its superior Li+ conductivity and diffusion coefficient of lithium ions much higher than those of the polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder. The calculated diffusion coefficient of lithium ions in WPUA is 2.43 × 10–12 cm2 s–1, which is twice times higher than that in PVDF. Employing the synthesized WPUA binder, the assembled LiFePO4@Li half cells show improved electrochemical performance of 110.8 mAh g–1 at 3C for over 800 cycles with 80.4% capacity retention and the high-loading LiFePO4@artificial graphite full cells also show improved performance of 135.0 mAh g–1 after 340 cycles with 87.1% capacity retention, both of which exhibit better electrochemical performance than PVDF. This work highlights controlled binder swelling as a key design parameter for balancing electrolyte accessibility, Li+ transport, and electrode integrity, offering useful guidance for the development of high-performance waterborne binders for lithium-ion batteries.

title: Poly-γ-Glutamic Acid-Modified Carbon Dots as an Enhanced Immune-Activating and Antigen-Delivering Nano-adjuvant for Improved Influenza Vaccine Efficacy
abstract: Abstract Vaccine adjuvants are essential components that enhance immune responses to antigens with limited intrinsic immunogenicity and shape the magnitude and quality of adaptive immunity. Although conventional adjuvants effectively stimulate innate immunity, their use is often limited by safety concerns or inefficient antigen delivery. Consequently, biologically derived and biodegradable biomaterials have gained attention as potent vaccine adjuvants. Among them, poly-γ-glutamic acid (γ-PGA) is a naturally derived biopolymer with intrinsic immunostimulatory activity that activates innate immune signaling and promotes cellular immune responses. However, γ-PGA alone shows limited antigen delivery efficiency, which can restrict formulation reproducibility and immune potency. Here, we report γ-PGA-modified carbon dots (PGA-CDs) as a rationally designed nano-adjuvant integrating γ-PGA-mediated immune activation with efficient antigen delivery. Compared with γ-PGA, PGA-CDs exhibited faster and more sustained cellular association, thereby inducing stronger dendritic cell maturation and proinflammatory cytokine production. They readily formed stable nanocomplexes with protein antigens, enhancing cellular uptake and antigen cross-presentation. In vivo, PGA-CDs formulated with ovalbumin elicited strong antigen-specific humoral and cellular immune responses. When combined with hemagglutinin (HA) from pandemic influenza A/California/04/2009 (pH1N1), PGA-CDs induced HA-specific humoral responses comparable to alum, while eliciting significantly stronger antibody and T cell responses than γ-PGA alone, resulting in complete protection against lethal viral challenge. Notably, HA/PGA-CDs also elicited more robust homosubtypic cross-reactive immunity than alum against influenza A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (H1N1), conferring complete protection. Furthermore, PGA-CDs were well tolerated in vivo, with no detectable hematological or histopathological abnormalities. Collectively, these findings establish PGA-CDs as a promising vaccine adjuvant platform that enhances antigen delivery, amplifies immune activation, and broadens protective efficacy.

title: Genesis of Nucleation Sites Dictates the Fate of 2D MoS2 Growth
abstract: Abstract Scalable synthesis of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) with atomic precision is critical for next-generation flexible electronics. Chemical vapor deposition is a primary strategy for the growth of 2D TMD films. The process, however, is difficult to control at large scales due to the strong interplay between time-dependent concentration gradients of the precursors, setup-specific fluid dynamics, and surface energetics. Here, we present a dual-channel reactor system that allows independent dynamic control over transition metal and chalcogen precursor dosages.
